works.title: A tumor suppressor function for prosurvival BCL-2 proteins in the thymus
works.abstract: Defective cell competition has been linked to tumorigenesis in various cancers, including acute lymphoblastic leukemia (T-ALL), but the underlying mechanisms remain unclear. In the thymus, we found marked elevation in the amount of prosurvival BCL-2 protein in “new” progenitors competing with “old” counterparts, suggesting an apoptotic mechanism. However, in a thymic transplant model of disrupted cell competition, Bcl2 deletion paradoxically accelerated the onset of leukemia resembling T-ALL. Mechanistically, the loss of BCL-2 did not alter competitive outcomes but induced heightened apoptosis and increased IL-7-driven compensatory proliferation in the surviving progenitors. This elevated cell turnover accelerated the acquisition of oncogenic mutations but did not change the mutational burden or landscape of T-ALL. More broadly, we found that even modest reduction in the related prosurvival proteins, MCL-1 or BCL-XL, also accelerated T-ALL-like disease in the transplant model. In a separate setting, conditional ablation of Mcl1 early in thymic lymphopoiesis caused profound thymocyte loss, elevated progenitor proliferation and spontaneous T-ALL. These findings define a tumor-suppressive function for BCL-2 family proteins in settings of defective cell competition, with important implications for the therapeutic use of BH3 mimetics in cancer.

works.title: Novel enzymes for amino acid biosynthesis in diverse bacteria and archaea: GapMind 2026
works.abstract: We previously described GapMind, an automated web-based tool for annotating amino acid biosynthesis pathways in bacterial and archaeal genomes. We used GapMind to identify gaps in biosynthetic pathways and systematically used comparative genomics and high-throughput genetics to identify candidate genes to fill these gaps. We confirmed the activity of ten of the proposed enzymes by using cross-species complementation assays. Highlights include a route to glycine via glyoxylate, two families that can replace phosphoserine phosphatase, an alternative N-succinyl-L,L-diaminopimelate desuccinylase, an alternative N-acetylornithine deacetylase, and a putative bifunctional MetB/MetC. We updated GapMind to include these additional enzymes. Across 208 prokaryotes that have high-quality genomes and can grow in minimal media, the average number of unexplained missing steps or gaps in amino acid biosynthesis dropped from 1.4 per genome to 0.7 per genome. The majority of remaining gaps involve the gain or loss of phosphate groups.

works.title: The optogenetic tool ASAP acutely inhibits autophagy
works.abstract: Abstract Autophagy, a conserved recycling process, manages intracellular quality control to mitigate stress. To determine the rapid effects of autophagy perturbation, we developed an optogenetic tool to rapidly inhibit autophagy, termed ASAP. Our approach leverages light-induced proteolytic cleavage to selectively inhibit autophagy within 5 min of light exposure, providing a precise and dynamic approach to study autophagy regulation. Proteomic profiling with ASAP revealed the most tightly regulated autophagy substrates along with previously unidentified substrates, including nuclear pore complex proteins. Of note, autophagy regulates quality control of cytoplasmic complexes of nucleoporins via specific LC3-interacting regions, sparing nuclear pore complex proteins embedded in the nuclear envelope. Upon rapid autophagy inhibition, incomplete nucleoporin complexes accumulate and instead of undergoing autophagic degradation, cytoplasmic nucleoporin complexes aggregate in processing bodies (P bodies). Using ASAP, we demonstrate rapid and specific inhibition of autophagy, revealing that nuclear pore complex proteins are tightly regulated autophagy substrates.

works.title: TMEM192 is a calcineurin-regulated membrane receptor for ubiquitin-independent lysophagy
Mapping mammalian placental formation and implantation transitions with single-cell transcriptomics and live imaging
Quantitative biophysical analysis of human septin hexamer and octamer self-assembly on model membranes
works.abstract: Septins are GTP-binding cytoskeletal proteins that shape and compartmentalize the plasma mem-brane. They assemble into heteromeric oligomers that further polymerize into filaments and higher-order structures. How differences between human septin hexamers and octamers influence the assembly of these membrane-associated structures remains an open question. Here, we address this question by using label-free methods to probe binding and self-assembly of recombinant human septins on supported lipid bilayers. Quartz crystal microbalance with dissipation (QCM-D) monitoring revealed that septin-membrane binding is diffusion-limited and concentration-dependent. Hexamers and octamers showed distinct viscoelastic properties, suggestive of structural differences. Imaging by atomic force microscopy (AFM) revealed that septin hexamers formed aligned nematic filamentous networks, whereas septin octamers formed aligned curved structures including spirals. QCM-D and AFM measurements both showed that septins form double-layered filament networks. However, upon C-terminal truncation of the SEPT6 and SEPT7 subunits, hexamers no longer bound the membrane while octamers formed a single-layered network of filament spirals. Our findings reveal that human septin hexamers and octamers interact differently with membranes, providing a baseline to understand their functions in the cell.

works.title: Saturation genome editing of BRCA1 across cell types improves interpretation of variant pathogenicity
works.abstract: Abstract Germline pathogenic BRCA1 variants predispose women to breast and ovarian cancer. Despite accumulation of functional evidence, over half of reported single-nucleotide variants in BRCA1 lack a definitive clinical interpretation. Furthermore, the consistency of variant effects across cell types remains largely unexplored. Here we performed saturation genome editing (SGE) of BRCA1 in HAP1 cells to score 4,113 previously unassayed variants. Additionally, we developed an SGE assay in human mammary epithelial cells (HMECs), allowing comparison of effects across cell lines, drug treatments and genetic backgrounds. We identified 538 variants impacting gene function through distinct mechanisms. HAP1 function scores discriminate between known pathogenic and benign variants with near-perfect accuracy. Intriguingly, however, nearly half of HAP1 loss-of-function variants scored neutrally in HMECs. We show that discordantly scored variants are hypomorphic and confer intermediate cancer risk. Overall, this work demonstrates how performing SGE across cell models improves the functional interpretation of rare variants.

works.title: PARP1 revisited — integrating DNA repair, replication and therapeutics
The Numb paradox: one protein, multiple isoforms, opposing functions in neurodevelopment, endocytic trafficking, and cancer
works.abstract: as an intrinsic determinant of asymmetric cell division, Numb's antagonism of Notch signaling has proven to be evolutionarily conserved in mammals, orchestrating the balance between progenitor maintenance and differentiation during neurogenesis. In the mammalian brain, Numb and its paralog, Numb-like (Numbl), integrate polarity cues, receptor trafficking, and transcriptional networks to guide cortical development and maintain neural stem cell homeostasis. Alternative splicing generates multiple Numb isoforms (i.e., p72, p71, p66, and p65) that exhibit distinct structural and functional properties, allowing context-dependent modulation of Notch, p53, and integrin pathways. Isoform-specific expression patterns underlie divergent roles in neurodevelopment, neurite morphogenesis, and tumorigenesis, whereby Numb can act either as a tumor suppressor or as an oncogenic driver. Dysregulated splicing, posttranslational modification, and interaction with RNA-binding proteins such as RBM4, PTBP1, or SRSF9 reprogram Numb's activity across developmental and cancer contexts. Emerging evidence also connects Numb isoform regulation to neurodegenerative processes, including tauopathies and viral neuropathogenesis, as observed in Zika virus infection. Collectively, these findings position Numb as a molecular switch at the crossroads of neurodevelopment, cancer, and degeneration with its isoform diversity providing both mechanistic insight and therapeutic potential for restoring differentiation, restraining oncogenesis, and protecting neuronal integrity.

works.title: Different lineages, one fate: convergent astrocyte differentiation in C. elegans
works.abstract: Astrocytes arise from molecularly distinct progenitors, yet how these lineages converge on a common glial identity remains unclear. In this issue of Genes & Development , Liu and colleagues (doi:10.1101/gad.353618.125) dissect this process in Caenorhabditis elegans CEPsh glia, which parallel functionally mammalian radial glia and its transition to astrocytes. CEPsh progenitors converge transcriptionally before postmitotic maturation. The CEH-43/Distal-less transcription factor acts as a terminal selector, directly regulating both the convergent embryonic program and the subsequent acquisition of mature astrocyte-like features. Comparative transcriptomics shows molecular similarities between CEPsh glia and mammalian astrocytes. These findings reveal a regulatory logic for convergent differentiation that could apply to other contexts.

works.title: Spatial transcriptomics defines segmental and temporal dynamics of pig intestinal epithelium
works.abstract: The pig ( Sus scrofa ) is widely studied as a large-animal model for human gastrointestinal biology, including gut physiology, pathology and disease. However, the spatial and developmental organisation of the pig intestine is not yet fully understood. Here, we generate a comprehensive spatiotemporal atlas of pig intestinal development by applying spatial transcriptomics to three intestinal segments across five developmental stages and an additional four intestinal segments at the adult stage. We identify spatial separation among enterocytes, plasma cells and stem cells, observing more pronounced separation in the small intestine compared to the large intestine. Pseudotime analysis of enterocyte-enriched regions reveals a gradient along the crypt-villus/crypt axis as early as post-conception day 70 in the jejunum, becoming fully evident across all intestinal segments by birth in the large intestine, with all three intestinal segments reaching a mature state by postnatal day 33. Our analysis indicates that the maturation of enterocytes during migration along the crypt-villus axis involves transcriptional programs similar to those governing enterocyte maturation across developmental stages, suggesting conserved molecular mechanisms governing both spatial and temporal differentiation. In the large intestine, nutrient transport-related gene expression declines progressively during development, transitioning from jejunum-like levels at early stages to markedly reduced levels in adulthood, consistent with functional specialization of distinct intestinal segments. Our study provides a high-resolution spatiotemporal framework of pig intestinal development and establishes a valuable resource for comparative biology and translational research.

works.title: Tachykinin-like NLP-58 signaling through TKR-1 modulates thermotaxis behavior in Caenorhabditis elegans
works.abstract: Neurokinin B (NKB) signaling plays a central role in mammalian thermoregulatory dysfunction associated with menopause, yet the underlying neural mechanisms remain incompletely understood. Here, we establish Caenorhabditis elegans thermotaxis as a genetically tractable system for investigating conserved tachykinin signaling. We demonstrate that overexpression of nlp-58, the C. elegans ortholog of mammalian NKB, induces abnormal thermotaxis behavior without impairing the temperature response of the thermosensory neurons. NLP-58 is expressed in multiple neurons, including the AIY interneurons, a central integrative node of the thermosensory circuit. AIY-specific overexpression of nlp-58 is sufficient to reproduce the thermotaxis defect, identifying AIY as an important site of NLP-58-dependent behavioral modulation. Genetic analyses further demonstrated that the thermotaxis behavior is mediated primarily through the tachykinin receptor TKR-1, the homolog of mammalian tachykinin 3 receptor (NK3R), acting in ASG and/or ASJ sensory neurons. We also identified a genetic interaction between dhs-4, a lipid metabolic enzyme gene, and nlp-58, suggesting that lipid metabolic pathway modulate tachykinin-dependent thermotaxis behavior. Furthermore, endogenous NLP-58/TKR-1 signaling contributed to the age-dependent decline in thermotaxis behavior. Finally, treatment with fezolinetant, a selective NK3R antagonist used clinically for menopausal vasomotor symptoms, partially improved the thermotaxis defect caused by nlp-58 overexpression. Together, our findings identify the NLP-58/TKR-1 signaling pathway as a modulatory component of thermotaxis behavior and provide a framework for investigating conserved principles of tachykinin-dependent circuit modulation.

works.title: A human-specific TAF8 isoform diversifies the composition of the TFIID general transcription factor
works.abstract: Despite its central role in RNA polymerase II transcription, the composition and function of the TFIID general transcription factor can vary across tissues and developmental stages. Such variability may provide a substrate for evolutionary innovation and contribute to human-specific regulatory functions. Here, we identify a human-specific short isoform of TAF8 (TAF8s), a scaffold subunit of TFIID, generated through the use of an intronic polyadenylation site (iPAS). Comparative genomic analyses reveal that the genomic substrate for this isoform originated with the insertion of a FLAM-C Alu element into intron 5 in the common ancestor of anthropoid primates (Simiiformes), whereas subsequent small sequence changes at the Alu-associated iPAS coincide with the emergence of TAF8s expression in the human lineage. TAF8s lacks nearly half of the canonical TAF8 coding sequence, is widely expressed across human tissues, and accounts for a substantial fraction of TAF8 transcripts. It encodes a truncated protein lacking the canonical nuclear-localization signal and localizes predominantly to the cytoplasm. Despite retaining interactions with its histone-fold partner TAF10 and other core TFIID subunits, TAF8s loses interaction with TAF2, providing a molecular basis for alternative TFIID sub-complex formation. Together, our findings identify a recently evolved human-specific regulatory innovation at the TAF8 locus that diversifies the composition of a conserved general transcription factor. This example illustrates how evolution of transcript isoforms can generate new protein interactions and molecular complexity in essential cellular machineries, with potential implications for the functional diversification of TAF-containing complexes and the genetic basis of TAF-related developmental disorders.

works.title: An RPEL-based FRET biosensor for free monomeric actin
works.abstract: Actin is critical for cell integrity and nuclear processes, but methods to visualise how environmental and intracellular signals affect cellular monomeric (G-) actin levels are lacking. We present the GASPs (G-actin sensing proteins), genetically encoded G-actin FRET sensors. Using cytoplasmic- and nuclear-localised GASPs, we show that in fibroblasts integrity of focal adhesions plays a critical role in maintaining low G-actin levels, and that cytoplasmic and nuclear G-actin levels increase at high cell densities and when spreading is restricted. Upon serum stimulation, it is depletion of the cytoplasmic G-actin pool that correlates with rapid nuclear accumulation of the MRTF transcription factors, whose subcellular localisation is controlled by G-actin. Stimuli that induce rapid increases or decreases in cytoplasmic G-actin level induce similar but slower changes in nuclear G-actin level, indicating that fluctuations in nuclear G-actin levels are largely subservient to cytoplasmic actin dynamics.

works.title: Identification of a novel anti-angiogenic regulatory sequence within the syndecan-3 extracellular core protein
works.abstract: Syndecans are transmembrane proteoglycans that regulate angiogenesis through their glycosaminoglycan chains and core proteins. We previously demonstrated that the syndecan-3 (SDC3) extracellular core protein possesses anti-angiogenic activity independent of its glycosaminoglycan chains. Here, using recombinant truncation mutants, endothelial migration assays and peptide mapping, we localised this activity and identified a minimal nine amino acid peptide, QM111, that retained full biological activity. QM111 inhibited endothelial cell migration and angiogenic sprouting in rat aortic ring and mouse choroidal explant models. Intrinsic disorder analysis revealed that QM111 resides within a region of comparatively reduced disorder, consistent with other syndecan regulatory sequences. QM111 did not induce inflammatory chemokine production, exhibited no detectable cytotoxicity, and retained substantial stability in human serum and vitreous humour. QM111 displayed anti-angiogenic activity comparable to the previously described syndecan-2-derived peptide QM107, with combination treatment producing robust inhibition of angiogenesis. These findings identify a novel anti-angiogenic regulatory sequence within SDC3 and support the concept that syndecan extracellular core proteins contain biologically active sequences with potential therapeutic utility.

works.title: Efficient count-based models improve power and robustness for large-scale single-cell eQTL mapping
works.abstract: This study presents jaxQTL, an efficient count-based pseudobulk single-cell eQTL mapping framework. When applied to OneK1K data, jaxQTL discovers more eGenes than existing methods while running faster.

works.title: The nucleocytoplasmic actin circuit in genome maintenance
Ultrafast alignment-free detection of viral genome variation with bronko
works.abstract: As viral sequencing datasets continue to grow, traditional alignment-based variant calling pipelines are becoming computationally prohibitive. To address these challenges, we developed bronko, an ultrafast alignment-free framework for detecting viral variation directly from sequencing data. The novel computational approach implemented in bronko allows scaling to massive viral sequencing datasets and has four key components: i) a locality-sensitive bucketing function to rapidly identify single-nucleotide polymorphisms (SNPs) relative to reference(s), ii) a direct k -mer count pseudo-mapping approach that approximates a pileup without alignment, iii) a greedy de novo assembly algorithm to reconstruct mutation-dense regions and indels and iv) a streaming-based sliding window outlier test to estimate baseline noise across the genome and precisely differentiate real minor variants from noise. Together, these components yield near-linear computational complexity with respect to sequencing depth, enabling bronko to process thousands of viral samples rapidly on modest hardware. Our results are threefold: 1) On simulated amplicon sequencing, bronko recovers variants with higher precision and comparable recall to existing tools while running up to one to three orders of magnitude faster; 2) bronko generates sequence alignments directly from sequencing data, with SNP content nearly identical to that of whole-genome alignment while also running in a fraction of the time, and 3) applying bronko to longitudinal sequencing data from chronically infected SARS-CoV-2 patients revealed consistent patterns of intrahost diversification and adaptive mutations over time. Altogether, these results demonstrate bronko's potential as a scalable tool for large-scale viral genomic analyses, overcoming longstanding computational barriers for intrahost and interhost characterization of viral variation.

works.title: Derivation of doxorubicin mutational signatures in cancer
works.abstract: Doxorubicin is a chemotherapeutic agent used for the treatment of solid and hematopoietic malignancies. Doxorubicin acts as a DNA intercalator and inhibits the topoisomerase II enzyme, leading to double-stranded breaks. We hypothesize that doxorubicin mutagenesis leads to a nonrandom pattern of somatic mutations on the genome, termed a mutational signature. We expose cells to doxorubicin using two different methodologies: (1) continuous exposure of a constant dose of doxorubicin and whole-genome sequencing of single-cell clones (previously published methodology) and (2) pulsed exposure of escalating doses of doxorubicin and whole-genome sequencing of a bulk population. We first confirm that the methodologies do not yield differing results through previously published cisplatin-exposed single-cell clone genome data compared with the dose escalation and bulk genome data. We then derive two doxorubicin signatures. The first, SBS-doxorubicin-1, is defined by an abundance of C > A mutations. The second, SBS-doxorubicin-2, is defined by a higher occurrence of T > C mutations. We then assess for the presence of our signatures within the genomes of patients treated with a doxorubicin-containing regimen. Across 10 bulk immune sorted samples from three patients with follicular lymphoma/diffuse large B cell lymphoma, as well as two metastatic samples from one patient with renal medullary carcinoma, we are able to detect both signatures in 83% of samples, with remaining samples harboring either signature. In summary, we experimentally derive two doxorubicin mutational signatures and demonstrate their presence in patient samples.

works.title: Short-read sequencing benchmarking with donor-specific assemblies
works.abstract: High-throughput short-read sequencing has become a core technology for genomics, but the rapid expansion of available platforms has made it increasingly important to benchmark them under standardized conditions. A major challenge is that conventional reference-based comparisons confound true sequencing errors with inherited variation and reference bias, making it difficult to isolate platform-intrinsic performance. We benchmark nine short-read chemistries across seven DNA sequencers using two highly characterized benchmark samples, HG002 and COLO829BL, together with donor-specific assemblies to measure sequencing errors against sample-matched genomic references. This strategy separates authentic platform errors from biological divergence and reveals substantial differences in substitution, indel, read-position, and sequence-context error profiles. Element AVITI UltraQ and Roche SBX-D show the lowest substitution error rates, whereas Ultima and Roche chemistries exhibit the strongest indel-associated biases. We find pronounced platform-specific effects in low-complexity regions and trinucleotide contexts, including homopolymer-associated errors and context-dependent substitution skews that are directly relevant to rare-variant detection. In addition, we show that donor-specific references are essential for unbiased base-quality recalibration because they minimize reference bias and more faithfully support cross-platform comparison and low-frequency variant-calling thresholds. Donor-specific assembly-based benchmarking provides a robust framework for measuring true short-read sequencing errors and comparing platforms on a common, sample-matched basis. Our results establish a comprehensive reference for the community and show that authentic error profiles can guide platform selection, quality filtering, and improved detection of rare somatic variation.

works.title: Microfluidic concatemer sequencing unveils cooperative and competitive enhancer clusters in gene regulation
works.abstract: Chromatin looping plays a pivotal role in eukaryotic gene regulation; however, technical limitations have hindered the comprehensive characterization of higher-order interactions among genomic loci. As a result, key questions, such as whether enhancers function cooperatively or competitively at the single-molecule and ensemble levels, remain largely unresolved. Here, we present Drop-t, a novel microfluidics-based method that enables systematic profiling of higher-order chromatin architecture at both the single-molecule and population scales. We demonstrate that Drop-t is not only resistant to common ligation-induced DNA entanglements, which frequently cause nanopore clogging, but also provides greater relevance for elucidating regulatory mechanisms compared to existing ligation-free approaches. Using Drop-t, we uncovered extensive, previously underappreciated non-specific enhancer-promoter interactions (EPIs) and showed that these may influence transcriptional variability by competing with specific EPIs. Notably, we identified two major gene classes, dictator genes and leader genes, based on whether their promoters are predominantly regulated by competitive or cooperative specific EPIs, respectively. Together, our findings established Drop-t as a powerful tool for decoding the higher-order organizational principles of chromatin architecture and their impact on transcriptional regulation and variability.

works.title: Bipartite DNA-binding domain of transcription factor BCL11B binds clustered short DNA sequence motifs
works.abstract: B-cell leukemia/lymphoma 11B (BCL11B), despite its name, is a key regulator of T-cell development, lineage specification, and T-cell malignancies. BCL11B contains a bipartite DNA-binding domain composed of two C2H2 zinc finger arrays: low-affinity ZF2-3 and high-affinity ZF4-6. These arrays recognize similar six-nucleotide motifs, TG(n)CC(n), as seven of the eight DNA base-contacting residues are conserved between them. The most conserved interactions involve the central GG dinucleotides, recognized by arginine and lysine residues at the key base-interacting positions of ZF3 and ZF5. We determined eight crystal structures of ZF2-3 bound to 12- or 20-base pair DNA duplexes containing either one or two binding motifs. The structures reveal that ZF2-3 recognizes DNA with remarkable configurational flexibility, binding motifs on either the same or opposite DNA strands with variable spacing in three relative orientations: head-to-tail (or tail-to-head), head-to-head, and tail-to-tail. Analysis of BCL11B ChIP-seq peaks revealed a strong enrichment of 1-bp-spaced, same-orientation TGACC(c/t) motif pairs. We also examined six neurodevelopmental disorder-associated missense variants affecting DNA base-contacting residues. Substitutions that replace bulky, positively charged arginine or lysine with smaller or hydrophobic amino acids weaken DNA-binding affinity and specificity, whereas substitutions between asparagine and lysine alter base recognition preferences.

works.title: Correction to ‘Different modes of engagement with the nucleosome acidic patch yield distinct functional outcomes’
Paralogous guanine deaminases acquired from bacteria by horizontal gene transfer promote purine homeostasis in Caenorhabditis elegans
works.abstract: Disruptions in purine metabolism contribute to a range of human diseases, from rare genetic disorders such as Lesch-Nyhan syndrome and xanthinuria to common conditions including gout and cancer. To better understand the metabolic networks that regulate purine homeostasis, we developed a Caenorhabditis elegans model of xanthine dehydrogenase (xdh-1) deficiency. Remarkably, xdh-1 mutant animals form rare xanthine stones, recapitulating a hallmark of human xanthinuria. To uncover genetic regulators of purine homeostasis, we performed a forward genetic screen for mutations that exacerbate xanthine stone formation in xdh-1 mutants. This approach identified multiple loss-of-function alleles in a previously uncharacterized gene, which we named gda-1. We show that gda-1 encodes an intestinal guanine deaminase that mediates a key enzymatic step in purine catabolism. The C. elegans genome also encodes a paralog, gda-2, which shares guanine deaminase activity but is expressed in distinct tissues. While gda-2 can compensate for gda-1 loss in guanine metabolism, the two genes exhibit non-redundant roles in regulating xanthine accumulation and stone formation. Interestingly, our evolutionary analyses suggest that gda-2 was acquired by nematodes via horizontal gene transfer from bacteria. These findings reveal a spatially regulated purine catabolism pathway in C. elegans and suggest that acquisition of bacterial genes has shaped a core nematode metabolic network.

works.title: Multispecies Mixtures: An Individual-Centered Quantitative Genetic Framework for Complex Plant Neighborhoods
works.abstract: Abstract Mixing crop species or varieties in the same field can raise yield and stability, but performance varies widely among combinations that breeders cannot yet predict. What makes a good neighbor is partly heritable, and quantitative genetics models this as an indirect genetic effect describing a genotype's contribution to its neighbors' phenotypes. Here, we extend existing models with a complementary approach based on continuous neighborhoods, in which diverse genotypes of two species are mixed. In a continuous-neighborhood design, several genotypes of each species are grown in a single trial, with every plant georeferenced. Each plant's phenotype is decomposed into direct genetic effects, indirect genetic effects from neighbors of both species, and environmental effects. Breeding values are then assembled for each genotype by combining its three genetic effects. We derived analytical expressions for the variances and covariance of these effects, validated the model, and evaluated its statistical properties through simulations spanning a wide range of parameter settings. For the same number of plants, the continuous-neighborhood design estimated indirect effects far more accurately than a pairwise design and, in addition, allowed indirect environmental variance to be estimated. Applied to a wheat–alfalfa experiment comprising 3,840 plants, from 181 wheat pure lines and 106 alfalfa families, the model attributed 8.6\% and 8.2\% of the variance in wheat grain number and alfalfa biomass to direct genetic effects respectively, and 4.0\% and 4.6\% to indirect genetic effects from alfalfa. The framework therefore offers an individual-centered basis for analyzing multispecies neighborhoods and their breeding potential.

works.title: A review-based guide to selecting an appropriate strategy for transgene-free genome editing in plants
works.abstract: The field of plant genetic engineering has advanced considerably since the development of the first transgenic crop plants, and even though transgenic varieties of various crops are now commercially available, consumer reluctance and environmental concerns over transgene escape pose limits on their expansion. Gene editing offers the opportunity to selectively and precisely alter DNA sequences without reliance on stably integrated transgenes, assuaging both concerns. Considerable progress has been made with the advent of programmable nucleases such as Cas9 and its derivatives. The transgenes encoding the gene editing components can be expressed transiently without integration in the plant's genome or removed from the genome via outcrossing or haploid induction to result in gene-edited plants that are no longer considered transgenic. Nonetheless, gene editing systems remain challenging to implement in some plant species, notably those that have long generation times or are vegetatively propagated, precluding the removal of editing tools through crosses. In these cases, a transgene-free method for introduction of all components needed to enable gene editing will bring the promise of modern breeding tools within reach. Transgene-free genome editing can be accomplished through the delivery of editing components as DNA, RNA, or ribonucleoproteins with delivery via Agrobacterium, microprojectiles, nanocarriers, DNA and RNA viruses, and grafting. Between technical constraints and scientific goals, it can be challenging to determine an appropriate transgene-free genome editing method. Following a review of the literature, a decision tree is provided to help select an appropriate method for a given plant species and to show how emerging tools, including smaller editors, can advance the field.

works.title: Large-scale structural analysis of pre-mRNA structure using RADIS
works.abstract: Pre-mRNA secondary structure can modulate the regulatory function of intronic sequences by masking or exposing splice-site signals and altering the accessibility of other features. Yet experimentally supported structural models for human pre-mRNAs have been largely restricted to splice-site-proximal sequences, leaving the deep intronic regions where ~70% of intronic disease-causing variants reside almost entirely unmapped. We developed RADIS (Reactivity Analysis of Deep and Intergenic RNA Structure), a strategy that yields strand-resolved chemical probing reactivity profiles across entire intron-rich loci by creating tiled arrays of RNAs that comprehensively span long genomic distances. This approach removes the abundance and locus-specificity constraints that otherwise limit pre-mRNA probing approaches. RADIS recovers known E. coli ribosomal RNA architectures and yields high-correlation with in-cell dimethyl sulfate (DMS)-MaP reactivities at representative splice sites (r = 0.87-0.90). RADIS-constrained folding of 109 5' and 88 3' splice sites uncovers an inverse relationship between base-pairing within the spliceosome footprint and splice-site strength, and partitions 81 branchpoints into three structural classes. Across 233 full-length Alu elements, sense Alu RNAs are more structured than antisense elements, and both partition into strand- and lineage-dependent structural classes. RADIS enables experimentally grounded structure analysis at disease-associated intronic and intergenic loci, complementing sequence-based variant-effect predictors.

works.title: The leader-trailer helix of pre-16S rRNA increases the speed and efficiency of 30S subunit biogenesis in Escherichia coli
works.abstract: Leader-trailer helices of precursor rRNAs are ubiquitous in bacteria and archaea and are crucial for ribosome biogenesis in Escherichia coli. Here, using an orthogonal ribosome system, we investigate whether an engineered protein-aptamer bridge can functionally substitute for the leader-trailer helix (hLT) of pre-16S rRNA in E. coli. We find that components of such a bridge, and even the 3' aptamer array component alone, can increase 30S subunit formation in the absence of hLT. Loss of RNase R or mutations of the degradosome (RNase E, PNPase, or RhlB) also boost 30S biogenesis in the absence of hLT. Quantification of orthogonal 16S rRNA suggests that these alterations act by stabilizing pre-16S rRNA molecules lacking the leader or trailer, giving sufficient time for rRNA folding to occur. In all cases, 16S rRNA level correlates with 30S subunit activity; however, the active fraction of 30S particles formed is substantially higher in the presence of hLT than in its absence. Notably, the complete set of aptamer-bridge components can fully stabilize pre-16S rRNA lacking hLT but fails to increase the active fraction of 30S particles formed. These findings suggest that hLT enhances both the speed and efficiency of 30S subunit formation in the cell.

works.title: Theoretical considerations regarding an acidic nanolayer surrounding lysosomes
A multi-tissue atlas of genetic regulatory effects in sheep
The integration of protein and organelle degradation systems and its pathophysiological functions
Community benchmarking of generative models for privacy-preserving synthetic bulk RNA-seq data generation
works.abstract: Abstract Background The synthesis of anonymized data derived from real-world cohorts offers a promising strategy for regulatory-compliant and privacy-preserving biological data sharing, potentially facilitating model development that can improve predictive performance. However, the extent to which generative models can preserve biological signals while remaining resilient to adversarial privacy attacks in high-dimensional omics contexts remains underexplored. To address this gap, the CAMDA 2025 Health Privacy Challenge launched a community-driven effort to evaluate synthetic and privacy-preserving data generation for bulk RNA-seq cohorts. Results Building on this initiative, we systematically benchmark 11 generative methods across two cancer cohorts (~ 1,000 and ~ 5,000 patients) over 978 landmark genes. Methods are evaluated across distributional fidelity, downstream utility, biological plausibility and empirical privacy risk, with emphasis on trade-offs between vulnerability to membership inference attacks and other evaluation dimensions. Expressive deep generative models achieve strong predictive utility and differential expression recovery, but are often more vulnerable to membership inference risk under the evaluated threat model. Differentially private methods improve resistance to attacks at the cost of reduced utility, while simpler statistical approaches offer competitive utility with moderate privacy risk and fast training. Conclusions Synthetic bulk RNA-seq quality is inherently multi-dimensional and shaped by trade-offs between utility, biological preservation and privacy. Our results indicate that model architecture drives distinct trade-offs across these axes, suggesting that model choice should align with dataset characteristics, intended downstream use and privacy requirements. Privacy risk should also be assessed using multiple complementary attack methods and, where possible, mitigated through formal differential privacy protection.

works.title: How microbes reprogram immunity through epigenetic and epitranscriptomic regulation
works.abstract: Abstract Microbial communities shape immunity through antigens, structural ligands, and metabolites, but how these transient signals are translated into stable, reversible, or disease-promoting immune cell states remains incompletely understood. This review examines epigenetic and epitranscriptomic regulation as interconnected layers of host-microbiota interactions. We discuss how microbial signals engage chromatin- and RNA-regulatory pathways across epithelial, myeloid, lymphoid, and stromal compartments, placing the microbiota- N 6 -methyladenosine (m 6 A) axis within the broader landscape of host and microbial RNA modifications. This framework helps explain how the same microbial molecule can promote barrier repair, immune tolerance, inflammation, or antitumor immunity depending on tissue exposure, responding cell type, and host state. We distinguish between association, microbiota dependence, and direct regulatory causality, and highlight knowledge gaps concerning non-m 6 A RNA modifications and bidirectional regulatory mechanisms. Finally, we outline key experimental and translational considerations, including microbial function, host target engagement, cell specificity, spatial delivery, and disease context. These insights highlight chromatin and RNA regulation as potential mechanistic links between microbial ecology and immune function that welcome further experimental investigation.

works.title: The effect of a reduction in population size on mean fitness and inbreeding depression
works.abstract: A sudden reduction in population size increases the rate of genetic drift, reducing variability and increasing the mean level of homozygosity. The resulting increase in exposure of strongly deleterious, recessive or partially recessive alleles to selection against homozygotes may lead to their being purged from the population, potentially allowing mean fitness to increase after an initial decline, and accelerating the decline in inbreeding depression associated with reduced variability. However, detailed population genetic theory on the effects of population bottlenecks on mean fitness and inbreeding depression remains limited. We develop a theoretical framework for small, randomly mating populations founded from a large population at mutation-selection-drift equilibrium, using both simulations and approximate analytical results. These provide quantitative predictions for the dynamics of the population's mean fitness and level of inbreeding depression following a bottleneck. In particular, we derive an approximate expression for the time needed for mean fitness to recover after an initial decline; such a recovery requires selection to be sufficiently strong relative to drift, and mutations to be sufficiently recessive. In contrast, weakly deleterious mutations cause reductions in mean fitness and inbreeding depression that are similar in size to those predicted from increases in homozygosity for neutral alleles, over the relatively short timescales considered here.

works.title: Author Correction: A tumour-resident Lgr5+ stem-cell-like pool drives the establishment and progression of advanced gastric cancers
Full-length RNA sequencing profiles intracellular and extracellular RNAs in euploid and aneuploid human embryos
Association of AXIN1 assemblies with microtubules inhibits Wnt/β-catenin signaling
works.abstract: The Wnt/β-catenin pathway is crucially involved in cell proliferation and differentiation. AXIN1, a key inhibitor of the pathway, scaffolds the β-catenin destruction complex in the cytoplasm, and pathway activation requires AXIN1 membrane recruitment and inhibition by DVL. Here, we discover an interplay of Wnt signaling and the cytoskeleton, mediated by direct binding of AXIN1 to microtubules via a positively charged binding site. The microtubule interaction ranges from peripherally attached AXIN1 condensates to tightly-tethered fibrillar assemblies that are inhibited by CK1-dependent phosphorylation. Microtubule binding renders the AXIN1 scaffold polymers more stable and stationary, favoring destruction complex assembly. It also counteracts the inhibition of AXIN1 through DVL, as shown by its impact on AXIN1 protein interactions and membrane recruitment, as well as on β-catenin degradation. Pharmacological or genetic inhibition of microtubule binding by endogenous AXIN1 activates Wnt/β-catenin signaling in several cellular systems. Moreover, a cell-permeable peptide designed to competitively block AXIN1 interaction with microtubules increases Wnt signaling and stimulates Wnt signaling-dependent differentiation of osteoblasts. In conclusion, AXIN1-mediated anchoring of the β-catenin destruction complex to microtubules suppresses Wnt signaling, suggesting a target for pharmacological modulation.

works.title: Purine metabolite accumulation suppresses mTORC1 through the TUFM-RHEB axis
Efficient and accurate mixed model association tool for single-cell eQTL analysis
works.abstract: Genetic effects on gene expression often vary across cell types, motivating expression quantitative trait loci (eQTL) mapping in single-cell RNA sequencing data. Existing approaches generally aggregate expression across cells, use Gaussian models poorly suited to read counts or do not scale. Here we show that SAIGE-QTL, a Poisson mixed model that directly models single-cell read counts, enables calibrated and computationally scalable eQTL mapping while accounting for donor-level and cell-level covariates and unequal numbers of cells per donor. In simulations and three single-cell datasets, SAIGE-QTL improved statistical efficiency and discovery of genes with significant eQTLs (eGenes) relative to pseudobulk methods and produced results consistent with existing single-cell models at substantially lower computational cost. In 1.2 million immune cells, SAIGE-QTL identified 48.8% more eGenes than pseudobulk analysis. SAIGE-QTL further enabled genome-wide trans-eQTL mapping and rare variant set-based testing, identifying rare variant associations independent of common eQTL signals. SAIGE-QTL therefore expands single-cell eQTL discovery across common, rare and trans-acting genetic variation.

works.title: Robust fine-mapping in the presence of linkage disequilibrium mismatch
Quantitative lineage tracing in mouse embryogenesis
MMEJ repair safeguards cancer ecDNA
Mapping somatic mutations in every corner of the genome
New neuronal microexons linked to autism
Bacterial protein function prediction via multimodal deep learning
works.abstract: Abstract Bacterial proteins are specialized with extensive functional diversity for survival in diverse and stressful environments. A significant portion of these proteins remains functionally uncharacterized, limiting our understanding of bacterial survival mechanisms. Hence, we developed Deep Expression STructure (DeepEST), a multimodal deep learning framework designed to accurately predict protein function in bacteria by assigning Gene Ontology (GO) terms. DeepEST comprises two modules: a multi-layer perceptron that takes gene expression and gene location as input features, and a protein structure-based predictor. Within DeepEST, we integrated these modules through a learnable weighted linear combination and introduced a novel masked loss function to fine-tune the structure-based predictor for bacterial species. These modeling choices are particularly well suited for bacteria due to the spatial organization of their circular genomes. Functionally related genes frequently co-localize and are co-transcribed within operons, allowing transcription dynamics to serve as crucial, condition-dependent regulatory signals. We show that DeepEST outperforms existing protein function prediction methods on a 25-species benchmark, relying solely on amino acid sequence or protein structure. Moreover, DeepEST predicts GO terms for unclassified hypothetical proteins across 25 human bacterial pathogens, facilitating the design of experimental setups for characterization studies. By combining expression, localization, and structure information in a unified deep learning framework, DeepEST bridges organism-specific data integration and structure-based transfer learning, providing a method tailored for bacterial protein function prediction in settings with structural and multi-condition expression data. Availability Accompanying code and data can be found under https://github.com/BorgwardtLab/DeepEST .

works.title: PmiREN3.0: a multi-omics integrated and AI-assisted encyclopedia for plant microRNA research
works.abstract: MicroRNAs (miRNAs) are key post-transcriptional regulators in gene regulatory networks (GRNs). Comprehensive research on miRNAs increasingly requires the integration of large and heterogeneous datasets, together with more efficient approaches to knowledge exploration. Here, we present PmiREN3.0, a major update of the Plant MicroRNA Encyclopedia. Compared with PmiREN2.0, species/subspecies coverage increased from 179 to 340, adding 22 orders, 51 families, and 108 genera. Using the same standardized workflow and annotation criteria as previous releases, high-confidence miRNAs were identified from 5319 small RNA sequencing (sRNA-seq) datasets, with miRNA loci increasing from 39 751 to 87 667 and miRNA families from 7838 to 18 389. Resources and tools from previous releases were extensively updated, while six new modules were added for primary transcripts, DNA methylation, RNA modifications, stress-responsive expression, metabolic pathways, and core GRNs. PmiREN3.0 also introduces miRai+, a knowledge service powered by artificial intelligence (AI) that combines a language model fine-tuned on miRNA knowledge with retrieval augmented generation. Evaluation yielded scores of 0.910 for answer relevance, 0.965 for faithfulness, and 0.906 for factual correctness. Together, PmiREN3.0 provides an expanded plant miRNA dataset and an integrated platform combining multi-omics data and AI-assisted knowledge services for plant miRNA research. PmiREN3.0 is available at https://pmiren.com/.

works.title: E2F1 induces a G0-G1 reentry transcriptional program without changing chromatin accessibility
works.abstract: Quiescent cells repress cell-cycle genes via chromatin-based mechanisms to maintain a non-dividing state, yet remain poised to reenter the cell cycle upon stimulation. E2F1, a canonical activator of cell-cycle genes, is sufficient to induce cell-cycle reentry from quiescence, but how it overcomes chromatin-mediated repression remains unclear. Here, we show that inducible E2F1 expression triggers exit from quiescence without changes in chromatin accessibility by harnessing regulatory elements with limited accessibility. Time-resolved transcriptomic analysis demonstrates that E2F1 induces an accelerated transcriptional program compared to serum stimulation. Unlike serum, which triggers broad chromatin remodeling, E2F1 activates genes within a chromatin context with limited accessibility. ChIP-seq analyses reveal that E2F1 binds target sites in quiescent cells to activate canonical cell-cycle genes. Biochemical reconstitution demonstrates that E2F1 binds nucleosomes and accesses DNA wrapped by histones. These findings suggest that E2F1 accesses nucleosome-associated DNA and initiates transcription without major chromatin reorganization. Our work redefines the relationship between transcription factor and chromatin dynamics during fate transitions and establishes E2F1 as a potent regulator capable of inducing cell-cycle reentry without changing chromatin accessibility.

works.title: Transcriptome- and methylome-wide association studies prioritized lung cancer genes in East Asian populations
works.abstract: The relationship between gene expression, DNA methylation, and lung cancer remains elusive in East Asian (EAS) populations. Transcriptome- and methylome-wide association studies (TWAS/MWAS) help uncover gene-trait associations by integrating multi-omics data, yet models trained mainly on European references limit cross-population generalizability. To address this, we developed EAS-specific gene expression and DNA methylation prediction models using whole-blood data from over 800 and 4,300 individuals, respectively. Applying these to lung cancer GWAS from Nanjing Medical University (13,327 cases; 13,328 controls) and Biobank Japan (4,444 cases; 489,012 controls), we identified 25 genes and 42 CpGs associated with lung cancer risk in the discovery stage, with seven genes and 32 CpGs replicated. Three novel genes outside known GWAS loci-RP11-57K17.1 (6q22.31), RP11-313J2.1 (10q11.21), and BMS1P2 (10q11.22)-were identified. In addition, Mendelian randomization analyses suggested that methylation-mediated downregulation of RP11-147L13.11 can reduce lung cancer risk. Our study reveals new susceptibility genes and offers insights into genetic-epigenetic regulatory mechanisms in lung cancer among EAS populations.

works.title: RNA-dependent aggregation of a common TEV protease variant alters in vitro biomolecular condensate reconstitution
works.abstract: Biomolecular condensates formed by liquid-liquid phase separation (LLPS) are commonly studied in vitro using protease-mediated removal of solubilizing tags to induce condensation under controlled conditions. Tobacco Etch Virus (TEV) protease is widely used for this purpose and is generally assumed to remain soluble and inert during condensate reconstitution. Here, we show that in RNA-containing systems, TEV protease variants can interact with RNA, leading to aggregation and changes in the phase behavior of the target protein. Using confocal microscopy, turbidity measurements, and mass photometry, we demonstrate that commonly used TEV protease variants differ in their propensity to undergo RNA-dependent aggregation. The widely used pRK793 TEV protease forms large RNA-associated aggregates. We further show that RNA-TEV aggregation alters the morphology and organization of protein-RNA condensates formed by well-characterized phase-separating proteins, including PGL-3 and FUS. Together, our findings show that TEV protease can directly impact in vitro LLPS assays through RNA binding and aggregation. These results underscore the importance of validating protease-based induction strategies and incorporating appropriate controls when reconstituting biomolecular condensates, particularly in RNA-rich systems.

works.title: Uplifting RNA Science in Africa: A Call to Action
works.abstract: The 21st century has witnessed the emergence of an entire new class of therapeutic and prophylactic medicines based on RNA. These transformative advances have arisen from decades of fundamental and applied research efforts to understand, exploit, and modify the properties of RNA to improve lives and livelihoods for patients and broader societal stakeholders. However, the contributions of African scientists, businesses and policymakers to the RNA research ecosystem have been minimal. This, despite the opportunities for exploitation of RNA-based medicines in specific health issues endemic to the region, such as the neglected tropical diseases schistosomiasis, lymphatic filariasis and Buruli ulcer, as well as chronic respiratory disorders (asthma, chronic obstructive pulmonary disorder) that disproportionately impact low and middle countries. Here, we outline some of the challenges faced by the incipient RNA bioscience research community in Africa, which remains hindered by a deficiency of strategic vision and insufficient momentum, an underdeveloped culture of collaboration, and persistent constraints in resources and infrastructure. Overcoming these issues requires a re-imagining of how the global RNA research community and African scholars mobilise resources for co-production of RNA-related knowledge and innovation. Potential solutions include forging equitable partnerships with institutions in the Global North, strengthening local, regional, and transnational collaborative networks in RNA science, and developing grassroots platforms that expand RNA education, research training, and communitywide networking across Africa. Together, these approaches offer a pathway to build sustainable capacity, nurture scientific leadership, and accelerate the growth of the continent's RNA bioscience ecosystem.

works.title: The evolutionary conserved protein-RNA interface formed by the cell-fate regulator Bicaudal-C
works.abstract: Bicaudal-C (Bicc1) is an essential cell-fate regulator that guides the animal body plan during early development and maintains organ homeostasis in adults. It does so by binding specific mRNA targets and regulating their translation, yet the molecular basis of mRNA target selection has remained unclear. Here, we combined experimental and computational approaches to define the Bicc1-RNA interaction. In vitro binding experiments with wild-type and mutant RNA substrates identified the RNA features recognized by Bicc1, while protein-RNA XL-MS-a UV-crosslinking approach coupled to LC-MS/MS-pinpointed Bicc1 amino acids in direct contact with RNA. Deep protein-sequence alignments showed that key RNA contacts are conserved across invertebrates and vertebrates, and binding experiments with recombinant Bicc1 proteins from multiple species confirmed this conservation functionally. AlphaFold 3.0 predictions of Bicc1-RNA complexes generated a structural model that complemented and extended these experimental findings. Together, these data establish that Bicc1 recognizes a bipartite binding site comprising a GAC primary sequence and a stem-loop structure through contacts distributed across both the KH1 and KH2 domains. This interface is conserved from invertebrates to vertebrates. This work thus defines the evolutionarily conserved mechanism by which Bicc1 selects specific mRNAs for translational regulation.

works.title: Author Correction: Divergent metabolic programmes control two populations of MAIT cells that protect the lung
works.abstract: In the originally published version of this article, an unintentional data-entry error occurred during the compilation of values for the OCR Klrg1 + group in Fig. 6j. Specifically, four numerical values (18.048268, 9.492484, 11.965342, and 22.810048) were duplicated within this group. The duplicate entries have been removed and the statistical analysis has been re-evaluated using the corrected data points. The recalculated P value (updated * P = 0.039) is reflected in the revised graph and the difference between the compared groups remained statistically significant. This clerical error does not alter any scientific conclusions of the figure or the overall findings presented in the manuscript. The original and corrected version of the panel in Fig. 6j are provided as Fig. 1 , below. This correction has been made to the HTML and PDF versions of the article. Fig. 1 Full size image Original and corrected Fig. 6j.

works.title: Author Correction: The formation of migrasomes is initiated by the assembly of sphingomyelin synthase 2 foci at the leading edge of migrating cells
DGKE acts as a negative regulator of podocyte migration and injury in glomerular diseases
SLC25A1/CIC supports osteoclastogenesis by coordinating mitochondrial bioenergetics and redox homeostasis
Multiscale multimodal integration of spatial omics through a deep generative model with CORAL
AI-guided cancer survival prediction could spare some children high-dose brain radiation
An information-theoretic framework for inferring T cell dynamics from single-cell RNA and T cell receptor sequencing
works.abstract: Single-cell T cell receptor (TCR) repertoire sequencing enables simultaneous profiling of gene expression and TCR sequences, providing a coregistered measure of T cell phenotypic diversity and clonal dynamics. However, principled probabilistic frameworks for joint modeling of clonotype and phenotype have remained limited. Here we introduce TCRi, a hierarchical Bayesian information-theoretic framework that infers the joint probability distribution between genetic clonotype and transcriptional phenotype from paired single-cell transcriptomic and TCR sequencing data. TCRi treats phenotype assignment as a probabilistic inference problem: a variational autoencoder embeds single-cell expression into a structured latent space, and a hierarchical Bayesian model learns clonotype-specific phenotype distributions through principled information-sharing across clonotypes, patients and covariates. From these distributions, TCRi computes information-theoretic quantities: clonotypic entropy, phenotypic entropy, phenotypic flux and mutual information between clonotype and phenotype. When TCRi was applied to four real-world datasets comprising 167,118 CD8 T cells from patients with cancer treated with anti-PD-(L)1 immune checkpoint blockade, mutual information emerged as a robust discriminator of therapeutic response.

works.title: Genome-wide scan for transmission ratio distortion in trios from the Norwegian MoBa cohort rules out moderate distortion at common variants
works.abstract: Abstract Transmission ratio distortion has been demonstrated in model organisms but is understudied in humans. We conduct single- and multi-locus transmission disequilibrium tests to detect transmission ratio distortion in up to 43,829 parent–offspring trios from the Norwegian Mother, Father and Child Cohort Study. We find little evidence for moderate to high levels of transmission ratio distortion at common variants. However, our multi-locus analyses implicate genes involved in meiosis, fertility, and prenatal development.

works.title: Ribocentre-FoldBridge: a comprehensive database bridging RNA chemical probing data and 3D structures
works.abstract: RNA chemical probing generates nucleotide-resolved profiles in vitro and in cells, while X-ray crystallographic or cryo-electron microscopy models provide high-resolution structural models but remain comparatively low throughput. Aligning these experiments from different modalities may provide insights into RNA structure formation and molecular functions. Here, we present Ribocentre-FoldBridge (https://foldbridge.ribocentre.org/), an AI-assisted, curator-reviewed database linking curated chemical-probing profiles with experimentally determined 3D structures. This database catalogues 12 types of RNAs, linking 256 929 probing profiles across five experimental categories to 5321 structure-linked cases. It interactively visualizes the probing profiles that align with RNA secondary and tertiary structures at nucleotide resolution. We demonstrate probe-specific reactivity patterns across paired, unpaired, and solvent-accessible structural contexts. The database aims to provide a reproducible evidence layer for examining RNA structure-function relationships across heterogeneous experiments, and thus facilitate the development of new RNA structure or function prediction programs.

works.title: R-loopBase v2.0: species- and cell type-resolved quantitative R-loop maps and R-loop regulatory resources
works.abstract: R-loops are non-canonical nucleic acid structures implicated in diverse cellular processes and diseases. We previously developed R-loopBase to address the pressing challenges of inaccurate R-loop maps and the limited understanding of the R-loop regulatory network. However, R-loopBase provided only human R-loop maps with categorical confidence and did not account for cell type specificity. These limitations, coupled with the emerging R-loop profiling technologies and advances in R-loop regulatory mechanisms, have motivated the development of R-loopBase v2.0 (https://rloopbase.nju.edu.cn). After uniformly re-analysing 358 R-loop mapping datasets generated by 16 technologies, we introduce a quantitative R-loop scoring framework that assesses genome-wide R-loop confidence in human, demonstrating strong concordance with known R-loop biology. We further extend the framework to specific cell types and mouse, fruit fly, and yeast. In parallel, we substantially expand the collection of R-loop regulators across species, enabling the inference of changes in R-loop homeostasis. Building on these expanded datasets, we implement several new interactive features and analytical tools, including an expanded multi-species genome browser, deep learning-based R-loop prediction, R-loop homeostasis analysis, and a streamlined data download portal. We anticipate that R-loopBase v2.0 will serve as an enhanced, up-to-date one-stop resource for the R-loop research community.

works.title: BioImage Archive: bringing bioimaging data together
works.abstract: The BioImage Archive (https://www.ebi.ac.uk/bioimage-archive) is EMBL-EBI's flagship resource for life sciences image data. It serves as a deposition database for biological images across scales from near-atomic through to whole organisms, and across imaging modalities. The Archive's mission is to support the reproducibility of quantitative results based on imaging, support methods development including modern deep-learning-based approaches, and allow large-scale reanalysis of image data. Across the Archive's ecosystem, we provide access to over 11 PB of image data. Recent developments in underpinning infrastructure now allow interactive exploration, visualization, and streaming access to a subset of the Archive's data using the new OME-Zarr file format, and will ultimately provide access to all of EMBL-EBI's archived image data, including data from the Electron Microscopy Public Image Archive. Migration of all holdings and a unified submission system are in progress.

works.title: The UCSC Genome Browser database: 2027 update
works.abstract: Since 2000, the UCSC Genome Browser (https://genome.ucsc.edu) has served as a standard tool for visualizing and comparing annotations across thousands of genome assemblies. Users can browse and visualize a wide range of data types from gene annotations to regulatory regions and comparative genome alignments. Once the data view is configured, the Genome Browser image can be exported for use in publications. Beyond visualization, users can use our tools to compare and export the annotations for further analysis. This year's feature updates include the full release of a tool to copy annotations between related assemblies, QuickLift; feature additions to our data-hosting service HubSpace to enable live editing of configuration files; two new display configurability options: "My Annotations" and custom item coloring; and several improvements to genome assembly discovery and track management. Beyond these new features, 28 new annotation tracks have been added across three broad categories: variant databases and interpretation, gene regulation, and transcriptome and gene expression. These include ENCODE4 cCREs and other ENCODE4 regulatory annotations, variant frequencies and phased variants from national sequencing projects, and two massively parallel reporter assay tracks.

works.title: OrganiZymeDB: a comprehensive database of enzyme stability and function in the presence of organic solvents
works.abstract: Low enzymatic tolerance to organic solvents is a major bottleneck for the development of industrial biocatalysis, since many substrates have limited water solubility, thus requiring the use of organic solvents for substrate solubilization and process economic viability. Yet, despite decades of experimental research in this field, no public resource currently exists that systematically collects and curates these data, limiting their accessibility and reuse for large-scale analyses and for the development and validation of computational methods. To address this gap, we present OrganiZymeDB (https://organizymedb.org/), a comprehensive, manually curated database of 28,121 experimental measurements of enzyme stability and function in the presence of organic solvents, compiled from 646 publications and covering 704 distinct proteins. Each entry is extensively annotated with the experimental conditions, including assay type, solvent identity and volume fraction, assay solution composition, pH, temperature, substrate(s), product(s), and enzyme production method, as well as the protein 3D structure and cross-links to other databases. OrganiZymeDB will assist both experimentalists, by providing straightforward access to solvent-compatibility data for enzymes of interest, and computational scientists, by providing a well-curated dataset to develop and evaluate methods for predicting enzyme solvent tolerance, ultimately enabling the design of robust industrial biocatalysts.

works.title: LncRNAfunc 2.0: an evidence-integrated knowledgebase for regulatory and functional interpretation of lncRNAs in cancer
works.abstract: Long non-coding RNAs (lncRNAs) play diverse regulatory roles in cancer, yet their functional interpretation remains largely based on molecular associations and computational predictions, while experimentally derived evidence is fragmented across heterogeneous resources. Here, we present lncRNAfunc 2.0, an updated knowledgebase for systematic functional interpretation of cancer lncRNAs through multi-source evidence integration. Compared with the previous version, lncRNAfunc 2.0 reprocesses pan-cancer data from The Cancer Genome Atlas, incorporates normal-tissue and cancer-cell-line contexts from GTEx and CCLE, substantially expands binding and interaction evidence, and introduces perturbation evidence for lncRNAs and their regulators. These resources are integrated with association-based analyses and computational predictions as complementary evidence for interpreting lncRNA-associated regulatory relationships. lncRNAfunc 2.0 organizes functional knowledge into six biological dimensions: dysregulation, upstream regulation, lncRNA-mediated mRNA regulation, transcript remodeling, protein regulation, and tumor phenotypes. This framework connects regulatory determinants of lncRNAs with their downstream molecular relationships and phenotypic associations, including mRNA regulation, alternative splicing, protein regulation, survival, molecular and immune phenotypes, and drug response. Overall, lncRNAfunc 2.0 provides an evidence-integrated framework for exploring context-dependent lncRNA functions and regulatory mechanisms across cancers. lncRNAfunc 2.0 is freely available at https://lncrnafunc.xu-bioinfo.com/.

works.title: GlyTouCan v4: a redesigned interface and expanded functionality for the international glycan structure repository
works.abstract: GlyTouCan (https://glytoucan.org) is the international, species-neutral glycan structure repository that assigns stable, globally unique accession numbers to glycan structures independently of the experimental method used to determine them. Here, we describe GlyTouCan version 4, released on June 22, 2026, which introduces a completely redesigned user interface with substantially faster browsing and searching, including a new "archetype" view that groups registrations that differ only in the anomeric or ring form of the reducing-end residue together for clearer filtering of the >256,000 glycans now registered. Version 4 provides an improved graphical structure input, via the updated browser-embedded GlycanBuilder application, for both searching and registering structures. Users may now sign in with an ORCID ID in addition to a Google account, and all previously released v3 REST API endpoints remain fully backward compatible. Version 4 also introduces a framework for industry affiliates, providing a structured pathway for commercial organizations that work with or synthesize glycans, while all existing academic database-partner relationships are maintained. GlyTouCan remains freely available to all users without charge, login, or registration for browsing and searching. We also summarize the repository's data content, which spans >600 monosaccharide types and, judging from these, includes many glycans of probable bacterial or plant origin.

works.title: iGPSC-DB: a comprehensive database for an inferred single-cell genetic perturbation atlas
works.abstract: Genetic perturbation-induced transcriptional reprogramming drastically remodels tumor cellular phenotypes and tumor microenvironment crosstalk. Unraveling the heterogeneous cellular responses to genetic perturbations is essential for the mechanistic dissection of tumors and the discovery of therapeutic targets. Here, we present iGPSC-DB (https://bio-bigdata.hrbmu.edu.cn/iGPSC-DB), a database designed to infer connections between tumor microenvironmental cells and diverse genetic perturbation events and to dissect the heterogeneous cellular responses to these perturbations. iGPSC-DB curates associations linking 178 114 perturbation events that target 7407 genes to 9 249 080 single cells from 1580 samples across 88 cancer types. iGPSC-DB also provides seven user-friendly tools for retrieving and analyzing: (i) inferred associations between genetic perturbation events and cells/cell types; (ii) the inferred perturbation-associated effects of perturbations on cellular functions, developmental trajectories, and cell-cell communication within the tissue microenvironment; (iii) the combined effects of different perturbations on cells, facilitating the design of combination therapeutic regimens; (iv) the impact of different perturbations on the differentiation trajectories and functional states of malignant cells; and (v) the association between perturbed target genes and clinical survival outcomes. iGPSC-DB will serve as a valuable resource to advance single-cell-resolution research on gene functions, regulatory mechanisms, and the discovery of tumor therapeutic targets.

works.title: Genomic ascertainment refines the population prevalence and phenotype associations of germline TERT variants
works.abstract: BACKGROUND: Individuals with deleterious germline variants in telomerase (encoded by TERT) are at high risk of pulmonary fibrosis (PF), liver disease (LD), bone marrow failure, head/neck squamous cell carcinoma (HNSCC), and other complications. Clinically ascertained cohorts are subject to biased ascertainment of affected individuals and families with early onset, complex disease. This study used genomic ascertainment to determine prevalence of deleterious TERT variants and the associated risks of telomere biology disorder (TBD) phenotypes. METHODS: TERT variants were extracted from exome sequencing data in UK Biobank (UKB, 469,377 exomes) and Geisinger-Regeneron DiscovEHR collaboration (DiscovEHR, 170,503 exomes). Cases were individuals with heterozygous deleterious TERT variants classified per modified ACMG/AMP criteria. Controls excluded rare, exonic, and splice site TERT variants. Electronic health records were assessed for TBD-related ICD10 codes. Case-control comparisons were done separately for UKB and DiscovEHR, accounting for smoking, alcohol, BMI, sex, genetic ancestry, and birthyear. RESULTS: There were 64 deleterious TERT variants in 203 UKB participants and 32 in 138 DiscovEHR participants. Prevalence estimates were 1:2,312 in UKB and 1:1,235 in DiscovEHR. Risk of PF was significantly increased for TERT heterozygotes compared with controls (UKB: odds ratio [OR] 10.9 95% confidence interval [CI]: 6.11-19.45, p < 0.001; DiscovEHR: OR 6.64, 95% CI: 3.31-13.3, p < 0.001). Deleterious TERT variants were also associated with higher risk of LD (OR 2.4, 95% CI:1.25-4.59, p = 0.038) and HNSCC (OR 5.75, 95% CI: 2.36-14.02, p = 0.001) in UKB but not in DiscovEHR. CONCLUSIONS: Rare deleterious TERT variants were present in 0.04 to 0.08% of the populations studied. Genomic ascertainment shows a predominance of pulmonary phenotypes, with PF associated with deleterious TERT variants in both cohorts. Associations with LD and HNSCC were observed only in UKB, possibly reflecting cohort differences including healthy volunteer bias. These findings illustrate the clinical importance of genetic diagnosis, and need for TBD-specific clinical trials.

works.title: PhytClust: Efficient and Optimal Monophyletic Partitioning of Rooted Phylogenetic Trees
works.abstract: Phylogenetic trees play a fundamental role in elucidating evolutionary relationships among taxa. Clustering taxa remains a major challenge across diverse biological domains such as cancer genomics, microbial systematics, and phylogenomics. Several methods partition taxa in phylogenetic trees into clusters, but these approaches face key limitations. Many rely on user-defined distance thresholds, whose choice often depends on prior knowledge and may be difficult to justify consistently across datasets. More broadly, existing methods often differ in how clusters are defined and commonly rely on heuristics or user-specified criteria to make the search space tractable for large trees. Here, we present PhytClust, a threshold-free algorithm that partitions trees into monophyletic subtrees (clusters) by identifying groups of taxa with low within-cluster dispersion. For a fixed number of clusters, PhytClust finds the exact global optimum under this objective and then selects the optimal number of clusters using a cluster-validity index. The resulting partitions are reproducible and reflect both tree topology and branch lengths. In simulated datasets, PhytClust outperforms existing methods in accuracy and remains competitive in speed while scaling to trees with more than a hundred thousand taxa. We apply it to viral and bacterial phylogenies, single-cell cancer phylogenies, archaeal and avian phylogenomics, gene family evolution, and plant conservation genomics. By providing a standardized method for partitioning phylogenetic trees, PhytClust yields partitions that are reproducible, exactly optimal under a stated objective, and computable on large trees.

works.title: A mixed expansion model of East Asian agriculture into northern Pakistan: demic via southern route but cultural from the northern
works.abstract: While East Asian agriculture notably impacted northern Pakistan's prehistory, its diffusion model into this region remains unclear. Here we generated 115 high-coverage whole-genome sequencing (WGS) data from three northern Pakistani populations (Burusho (Hunza), Shina, and Hazarewal), and integrated 2,029 modern and 4,358 ancient genomes from Eurasia. Our results revealed genetic input from East Asia into northern Pakistan, which, albeit with small proportions, contributed to shaping the genetic landscape of both ancient and modern populations in this region. We identified two distinct waves of East Asian ancestry into northern Pakistan-one introduced by rice farmers from the Yangtze River Basin ∼4,800 years ago and a second, ∼1,600 years ago, likely introduced by Tibetan Plateau population historical expansions -both via the southern foothills of the Tibetan Plateau. In contrast, our analyses provided no clear evidence of the tested ancestries associated with the northern Inner Asian Mountain Corridor. We thus propose a mixed model of East Asian agricultural dispersal into northern Pakistan, involving demic diffusion along the southern route, with cultural diffusion as a plausible explanation for the northern route.

works.title: The series of genetic codes that preceded our own
works.abstract: We produce a working hypothesis for the steps by which the canonical genetic code might have been constructed. We assume amino acids were added in the order inferred from their enrichment or depletion in ancestrally reconstructed sequences dating back to the Last Universal Common Ancestor (LUCA) relative to that in ancient but post-LUCA controls. To convert this ordering into a time series of 64-codon genetic codes, we followed the "2-1-3 rule" that information appeared first at the middle codon position, then mostly at the first before the third, with purine vs pyrimidine distinctions tending to precede distinctions between purines or between pyrimidines. Two notable deviations from the 2-1-3 rule suggest an ancestral promiscuity between valine/isoleucine/methionine, and between alanine/threonine, to produce "statistical proteins." The same promiscuities enable amino acids to be added in order of appearance at successive nodes in the cladograms of Class I and Class II aminoacyl-tRNA synthetase catalytic domains. Trifonov's previous amino acid ordering did not produce this consilience, with both a worse fit to the 2-1-3 rule, and discordance of synthetase trees with the order. More support for late resolution of hydrophobic promiscuity comes from post-LUCA differentiation between the synthetases of valine and isoleucine, in a manner dependent on 2 conserved tryptophans. The observed promiscuous activities of synthetases, and deep mutational scanning data on which amino acid substitutions are best tolerated, also align well with our reconstructed time series of genetic codes. As a working hypothesis, this series can guide research on random peptides, urzymes, and substitution models.

works.title: High-resolution Analysis of Magnesium Ions in Ribosomes across Species and rRNA Modification States
works.abstract: With advances in structural biology, particularly cryogenic electron microscopy (cryo-EM), ribosome structures at increasingly high resolution have become available. These datasets enable detailed analysis of features that were previously inaccessible, such as ribosome-associated metal ions. Among these, Mg²⁺ plays a critical role in stabilizing the ribosome and supporting translation.
