In this study, we analyzed high-resolution structures of the large subunit from three organisms, including variants lacking specific rRNA chemical modifications. We found that Mg²⁺ distributions are largely conserved across species and modification states within highly conserved regions. However, we also observed differences in conserved but peripheral regions, as well as near 2'-O-methylation and pseudouridine sites upon loss of these modifications. In addition, we identified cases in which arginine or other positively charged residues of eukaryote-specific proteins in human ribosomes appear to substitute for Mg²⁺ ions present in bacterial ribosomes. Together, these findings are consistent with a well-conserved core and highlight a role for eukaryote-specific features in shaping Mg²⁺ distributions.

works.title: Positional replication fork instability drives PARP inhibitor cytotoxicity
Tau monomers and fibrils escape microglial clearance via distinct cellular mechanisms
works.abstract: Tauopathies, such as Alzheimer's disease, are neurodegenerative disorders characterized by the accumulation and propagation of toxic extracellular forms of the microtubule-associated protein tau across brain regions. Microglia, the resident macrophages of the brain, are known for clearing and degrading toxic proteins. However, emerging evidence suggests that microglia also enhance tau spreading. To dissect the molecular mechanisms underlying microglial responses to extracellular tau, we use high-resolution imaging and biochemical approaches to assess the trafficking dynamics of different extracellular tau species in human induced pluripotent stem cell-derived microglia. Here we find that tau monomers are internalized by microglia via cell-surface LRP1 receptors but fail to reach terminally degradative lysosomes; instead, they are persistently recycled back to the extracellular space. In contrast, tau fibrils are not internalized and primarily adhere to the cell surface through an HSPG-dependent mechanism, triggering TLR4-mediated microglial activation and the release of pro-inflammatory cytokines. Heparin or anti-tau treatments dampen tau fibril-mediated microglial activation. In addition, disease-associated variants of the Alzheimer's disease-related protein APOE reduce microglia-tau interactions, further reducing tau uptake. Together, these findings demonstrate that microglia fail to efficiently clear extracellular tau monomers and fibrils through mechanistically distinct cellular processes, emphasizing the need for tailored therapeutic strategies to enhance extracellular tau clearance in neurodegenerative diseases.

works.title: Human REXO4 is Required for Cell Cycle Progression
works.abstract: Human REXO4 is a poorly characterized exonuclease that is overexpressed in human cancers. To better understand the function of REXO4 and its relationship to cellular proliferation, we have undertaken multidisciplinary approaches to characterize its cell cycle phase-dependent subcellular localization and the cis determinants required for this localization, its importance to cell cycle progression and cell viability, its protein-protein association network, and its activity. We show that the localization of REXO4 to the nucleolus in interphase depends on an N-terminal nucleolar localization sequence and that its localization to the perichromosomal layer of mitotic chromosomes is dependent on Ki67. Depletion of REXO4 leads to a G1/S cell cycle arrest, and reduced cell viability. REXO4 associates with ribosome components and other proteins involved in RNA metabolism. Overall, our results show that REXO4 is dynamically localized to distinct RNA-containing structures throughout the cell cycle, associates with RNA metabolism proteins, and is required for proper cell cycle progression and cell viability.

works.title: The reticulon homology domain of Pex30 generates membrane curvature at ER subdomains for lipid droplet biogenesis
works.abstract: Lipid droplets (LDs) are dynamic organelles that store neutral lipids and form in the endoplasmic reticulum (ER) membrane. Formation of new LDs is a controlled process and requires proteins with specific functions to form and grow from the ER membrane without any defect. In vitro studies have suggested a role for membrane curvature in LD emergence from the ER. Here, we use the reticulon-like membrane-shaping protein Pex30 to investigate the impact of ER membrane curvature on LD biogenesis and morphology. We modified the reticulon homology domain (RHD) of Pex30, which is responsible for tubulating the ER membrane, by extending the short hairpin transmembrane domains (TMD). The Pex30 (TMD) mutants cannot tubulate the ER membrane and generate less local membrane curvature than WT Pex30. Additionally, these mutants are unable to restore delayed LD biogenesis observed in cells devoid of Pex30. Our results indicate that Pex30 RHD generates local membrane curvature at ER subdomains that drives formation of new LDs.

works.title: Autoinhibition of heterotrimeric kinesin-2 is essential for ciliogenesis
works.abstract: The heterotrimeric kinesin-2 motor (KIF3A/KIF3B/KAP3) drives anterograde intraflagellar transport and is essential for mammalian ciliogenesis. A recent study has proposed a structural model for heterotrimeric kinesin-2 autoinhibition and provided initial functional support, but the basis of this regulation and its consequences in cells remain incompletely defined. Here, using structure-guided cell-based assays and knockout-rescue experiments with chimeric KIF3A and KIF3B subunits, we define key determinants of kinesin-2 autoinhibition. Subunit-specific interactions between the motor domains and the C-terminal coiled-coil and adjacent tail β-hairpin regions stabilize the autoinhibited state. The same C-terminal elements are also required for stable heterodimerization. We further identify a flexible region within the stalk coiled-coil that is required for autoregulation. Chimeras with strongly disrupted autoinhibition fail to support ciliogenesis, whereas partially impaired chimeras support ciliogenesis inefficiently and accumulate prominently at ciliary tips. These findings show that heterotrimeric kinesin-2 autoinhibition is critical for ciliogenesis and proper ciliary motor distribution.

works.title: Functional Interaction of SKA and NDC80 Complexes at Kinetochores Promoting Anaphase Onset in Mitosis
works.abstract: The spindle and kinetochore associated (SKA) and NDC80 complexes are essential kinetochore elements that ensure highly accurate chromosome segregation and successful progression through mitosis. The SKA heterotrimeric complex consists of SKA1, SKA2, and SKA3 subunits, and the NDC80 complex contains NDC80, NUF2, SPC24, and SPC25 subunits. Through live cell fluorescence timelapse imaging assays and expression of RNAi-resistant SKA3 constructs, we rescue SKA complex function in cells lacking endogenous SKA3. These assays reveal a critical span within SKA3’s C-terminus required for successful mitotic progression. Structural protein modeling shows that this span encompasses the majority of a roughly 40 amino acid SKA3 C-terminal structural element predicted to promote interaction with the coiled-coil NDC80 and NUF2 subunits of the NDC80 complex. Thus, although spindle and kinetochore concentration of the SKA complex is mediated in part by the tubulin and tip-tracking capabilities provided by the SKA1 component of the SKA complex, the transition from metaphase to anaphase requires residues of the C-terminal region of SKA3, likely due to their role mediating interaction between SKA and NDC80 complexes.

works.title: Hypoxia Promotes Wound Healing via Dynamical-Mechanical Balance and Adhesion Remodeling
works.abstract: Wound healing is a tightly orchestrated physiological process governed by dynamic cell-cell and cell-matrix interactions, yet how hypoxic microenvironments regulate migratory behavior in cells with latent lineage plasticity remains incompletely understood. Here, using HEK293T and MDCK cells as a genetically tractable model, we investigated the cellular and molecular mechanisms driving hypoxia-accelerated collective wound repair. Time-lapse live-cell imaging and morphometric analyses revealed that hypoxic exposure significantly accelerated migration, shifted cell cycle progression toward the S/G2/M proliferative phases, and induced pronounced morphological spreading. Pharmacological inhibition of cell division using mitomycin C abolished hypoxia-induced wound closure, highlighting the importance of cell proliferation in this wound closure process. In addition, hypoxia induces persistent downregulation of DSG2, while ITGB3 exhibits a distinctive biphasic kinetic response characterized by an initial upregulation followed by a sustained decline. Transcriptomic analysis indicated shifts in gene expressions related to cell-cycle transition, cell junctions, and cell adhesion upon hypoxia treatment. Collectively, our findings elucidate a cooperative interplay between proliferation-driven cell movement and cell-cell and cell-matrix adhesion remodeling under hypoxia to facilitate tissue repair. works.title: Development of a tryptophan-based dual selection system to investigate S-layer spatial organization during cytokinesis in Sulfolobus acidocaldarius
works.abstract: Sulfolobus acidocaldarius is a thermoacidophilic archaeon used as a model system for studying fundamental cellular processes and for emerging biotechnological applications. However, the limited availability of selectable markers restricts advanced genetic manipulation in this organism. Here, we report the development of a tryptophan auxotrophy-based selection system in S. acidocaldarius . A Δ trpBA mutant was constructed in the Δ pyrE background strain using a classical pop-in/pop-out recombination strategy. The resulting mutant exhibited little impairment of growth in rich medium, likely due to exogenous tryptophan supplied by complex nutrients, but failed to grow in a newly developed defined Brock-based amino acid dropout medium lacking tryptophan. Exploiting both uracil and tryptophan auxotrophies, we achieved dual-plasmid co-transformation and co-expression of the surface layer proteins and a dominant-negative mutant of the AAA-ATPase Vps4, revealing the accumulation of surface layer lattice forming protein SlaA at the midzone of division-arrested cells and its membrane anchor SlaB. Together, these results provide evidence for spatial regulation of S-layer assembly during archaeal cytokinesis while expanding the genetic toolkit available for S. acidocaldarius .

works.title: ENPP1 inhibits the cGAS–STING pathway to mediate immune evasion in EGFR-TKI–resistant non–small cell lung cancer
works.abstract: Third-generation EGFR tyrosine kinase inhibitors (TKIs), such as osimertinib, have demonstrated promising clinical efficacy in the treatment of EGFR-mutant non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC). Despite substantial progress with EGFR-TKIs, the development of acquired resistance remains a major clinical challenge. Notably, the addition of immune checkpoint blockade after TKI resistance has not resulted in significant survival benefits compared to chemotherapy. In this study, we performed a comprehensive transcriptomic analysis of established osimertinib-resistant tumor models and found that the expression of the ectonucleotide phosphodiesterase ENPP1, a key regulator of extracellular cGAMP signaling, was significantly upregulated in resistant tumors compared to the parental TKI-sensitive NSCLC tumors. Mechanistically, upregulated ENPP1 in resistant cells promoted the hydrolysis of extracellular cGAMP, suppressing the cGAS-STING pathway in immune cells and subsequently impairing immune cell activation and function, thereby promoting immune suppression and tumor progression. Genetic depletion or pharmacological inhibition of ENPP1 enhanced immune cell-mediated cytotoxicity against TKI-resistant tumor cells. Furthermore, the use of ENPP1 inhibitors both in vitro and in vivo enhanced immune cell activity and antitumor efficacy in TKI-resistant lung cancers with high ENPP1 expression. Importantly, these observations were further validated by paired clinical tumor samples, which demonstrated increased ENPP1 expression following the development of acquired EGFR-TKI resistance. Collectively, our study highlights a critical role for ENPP1 in mediating immune evasion through suppression of the cGAMP-STING pathway in the tumor immune microenvironment, supporting ENPP1 as a promising therapeutic target to enhance immunotherapy efficacy in EGFR-TKI-resistant NSCLC.

works.title: JNK signalling balances apoptosis and cell survival during tissue stress
works.abstract: Recovery from tissue stress requires the elimination of damaged cells and the commensurate production of healthy cells. How these two processes are coordinated to ensure tissue recovery remains poorly understood. Here we show that the c-Jun N-terminal kinase (JNK) pathway orchestrates apoptosis and proliferation, two seemingly opposite cellular behaviours, in response to epithelial stress. We took advantage of new optogenetic tools to trigger a pulse of JNK signalling activity in a defined domain of Drosophila wing primordia and mapped the response in time and space. Within 3 h after induction, the cells within the activation domain arrest proliferation, while a subset undergo apoptosis. As JNK signalling returns to background level, apoptosis subsides and proliferation resumes to allow completion of development with high fidelity. Using a sensitive reporter, we find that while JNK triggers apoptosis, the level of JNK activity does not correlate with apoptosis on a cell-by-cell basis. We show that the cell cycle phase modulates the pro-apoptotic activity of JNK signalling: G2 arrest is protective, while, in G1, mild JNK signalling activity suffices to trigger apoptosis. Transcriptomic analysis identified the genes encoding Dally and Dally-like protein (Dlp) among the most upregulated by excess JNK signalling. We show that these glypicans contribute to tissue repair by enhancing surface retention of the ligands Wingless (a Wnt) and Dpp (a BMP). We suggest that the resulting local increase in morphogen signalling provides subsequent protection from the pro-apoptotic effect of JNK signalling, allowing surviving cells to re-enter the cell cycle and resume development. Accordingly, recovery from ribosomal protein deficiency or irradiation-induced stress is impaired upon reduction of Dlp activity. Our work shows how a single stress pathway can selectively trigger apoptosis while protecting cells that can contribute to tissue recovery during resumption of normal development.

works.title: Longitudinal single-cell profiling of breast tumors highlights immune and epigenetic mechanisms associated with sensitivity to aromatase inhibitors
works.abstract: Estrogen receptor (ER)-positive breast cancer treatment is based primarily on endocrine therapy. To dissect mechanisms of sensitivity to aromatase inhibitors in ER-positive breast cancer, we profiled tumor biopsies from 25 patients during neoadjuvant therapy using single-cell RNA sequencing, immune receptor sequencing and enhancer activity mapping. Malignant cells with high ER signaling and elevated activity of enhancers with ER binding sites were sensitive to treatment. Resistance was associated with androgen receptor signaling, dedifferentiation and epithelial–mesenchymal transition. Poor responders preferentially used the androgen receptor cis-regulome under treatment pressure. The baseline tumor microenvironment was associated with tumor downstaging. Poor responders exhibited a ‘hot’, yet ineffective immune landscape enriched for naive lymphoid and undifferentiated myeloid cells. Good responders showed an active immune microenvironment with sustained clonal expansion of T cells. Our longitudinal single-cell analyses elucidate the genetic, cellular and epigenetic mechanisms driving sensitivity and resistance to neoadjuvant aromatase inhibition in ER-positive breast cancer. This longitudinal single-cell study of estrogen receptor (ER)-positive breast cancer suggests that strong estrogen signaling, ER-linked enhancers and active T cell responses could predict sensitivity to aromatase inhibitors, whereas resistance involves androgen signaling though hormone-sensing enhancer activity.

works.title: The Participant Engagement and Cancer Genome Sequencing Network to accelerate research in rare and understudied cancers
authors: On behalf of the Participant Engagement and Cancer Genome Sequencing (PE-CGS) Network

works.title: Fast and accurate resolution of ecDNA sequence using Cycle-Extractor
works.abstract: Extrachromosomal DNA (ecDNA) plays a key role in cancer pathology. ecDNAs mediate high oncogene amplification and expression and are associated with worse patient outcomes. Accurately determining the structure of these circular molecules is essential for understanding their function, yet reconstructing ecDNA cycles from sequencing data remains challenging. We introduce Cycle-Extractor (CE) for this task. CE takes as input a breakpoint graph derived from either short or long read sequencing data and extracts cycles of maximum length-weighted copy number. CE utilizes a mixed-integer linear program (MILP) and a separate traversal procedure, enabling fast optimization and compatibility with open-source ILP solvers. We evaluated CE against CoRAL (long-read, mixed-integer quadratically constrained programming), Decoil (long-reads), and AmpliconArchitect (AA; short reads) on both simulated data and real cancer cell lines. On simulated ecDNA, CE achieves accuracy comparable to CoRAL across three metrics and consistently outperforms AA and Decoil. On cancer cell lines, CE produces longer and heavier cycles than AA, and performs comparably to CoRAL, while being on average 40× faster. These results demonstrate that CE accurately reconstructs ecDNA from both short and long-read sequencing data, and that long-read inputs allow CE to recover more complete, higher-confidence ecDNA structures. CE improved the prediction of many ecDNA structures. On PC3 ecDNA containing MYC, CE uses ONT data to reconstruct a substantially larger and higher-copy sequence (4.2 Mbp) compared to the short-read-derived reconstruction (690 kbp). CRISPR-CATCH experiments confirm the presence of a large ecDNA molecule, validating the long-read-based CE reconstruction.

works.title: ECOD in 2027: a modernized interface and an updated classification of protein domains
works.abstract: The Evolutionary Classification of Domains (ECOD) organizes protein domains into a hierarchy of evolutionary relationships, encompassing both experimentally determined and computationally predicted structures. ECOD now classifies 2.9M domains, of which ∼1.37M derived from the Protein Data Bank and 1.51M from predicted models in the AlphaFold Protein Structure Database. The principal development we report here is a complete rebuild of the ECOD web resource. Search has been reconstructed around three modalities: (i) sequence, (ii) structure, and (iii) keyword. Foldseek now is the primary search method for the ECOD web page, searching a ∼457k representative domain database that is also distributed for local use. Results are presented through a Mol* interactive viewer, and a new API has been developed for programmatic access to the database. Alongside the interface, the pipeline for classifying new PDB entries has been rebuilt and returned to a regular cadence, family groups have been synchronized with Pfam v38.2, the bulk distributables have been reorganized and now include the search databases, the ligands in contact with each domain are recorded for experimental structures and annotated with drug cross-references from DrugDomain, and a registry has been introduced through which ECOD assigns stable identifiers to gene-called proteins and records the structures it predicts. ECOD is freely available at http://prodata.swmed.edu/ecod.

works.title: Correction to ‘Conformational reorganization and phase separation drive hyper-editing of ADR-2–ADBP-1 complex’
Tetraspanin CD81 restricts Ebola virus infection and is antagonized by glycoprotein GP and matrix protein VP40
works.abstract: Viruses manipulate host cell membranes to evade antiviral immunity, prevent superinfection, and optimize their replication and spread. The Ebola virus glycoprotein GP mediates viral entry but also contributes to the subversion of host antiviral immune responses. Here, we characterize the impact of Ebola virus GP on cell surface proteins and show that it reduces cell surface availability of tetraspanins CD81, CD63, and CD9. This function is conserved among several filoviral glycoproteins but not observed for glycoproteins of other viral families. Whereas CD63 and CD9 are largely dispensable for Ebola virus replication, CD81 suppresses virus-like particle entry and viral replication. This activity might be attributed to CD81-mediated suppression of NF-κB signaling, which is induced by the Ebola virus matrix protein VP40 and transcription- and replication-competent virus-like particle (trVLP) replication. Our results further indicate that both GP, which interacts directly with CD81, and VP40, which also associates with CD81, function to reduce total and surface expression levels of CD81. CD81 is shown to reduce levels of Ebola virus RNA species, and its antibody-mediated clustering can suppress Ebola virus infection. Our study provides insights into the roles of NF-κB signaling in Ebola virus replication and immunopathogenesis, and identifies tetraspanin CD81 as a potentially druggable Ebola virus-inhibitory host factor.

works.title: XGBoost-SHAP analysis prioritizes lower-frequency variants predicted to affect HNF4A binding motifs in pancreatic progenitors
works.abstract: BACKGROUND: Noncoding genetic variants underlie many complex traits, yet predicting their regulatory impact in cell type-specific contexts remains a major challenge. Transcription factor binding is a primary mechanism through which noncoding variants influence gene regulation, but the relationships among chromatin accessibility, variant frequency, and transcription factor binding are complex and nonlinear, limiting the performance of traditional linear models. METHODS: We generated single-nucleus ATAC sequencing data from seven induced pluripotent stem cell-derived pancreatic progenitor cell samples and identified 93,803 heterozygous single nucleotide polymorphisms overlapping accessible chromatin regions. Allele-specific effects (ASE) were quantified for each variant via binomial tests. We trained XGBoost, logistic regression, and regularized logistic regression models to predict allele-specific effects via chromatin read depth, peak score, variant minor allele frequency (MAF), and transcription factor binding prediction for five pancreatic transcription factors: HNF4A, HNF1A, NEUROD1, NKX6-1, and PDX1. Model performance was assessed by the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) via fivefold cross-validation as well as using test and validation SNP sets. Shapley (SHAP) value analysis was used to interpret model predictions and to cluster variants on the basis of their regulatory feature contributions. RESULTS: XGBoost significantly outperformed linear models, particularly at stringent allele-specific effect thresholds, consistent with its ability to capture nonlinear interactions among features. Chromatin read depth, peak score, and minor allele frequency were the strongest predictors. Stratification by read-depth and MAF deciles showed that XGBoost retained better overall predictive performance across deciles than the linear models, indicating that its advantage was not explained by these variables alone. Dimensionality reduction of variants on the basis of Shapley value profiles revealed seven clusters with distinct chromatin states and variant allele frequencies. These findings were supported by highly significant pairwise differences in allele frequency distributions across the seven clusters. One cluster was enriched for lower-MAF SNPs showing strong predicted interactions with HNF4A binding motifs. Because MAF and its SHAP contribution were inputs to the embedding, the lower-MAF identity of this cluster was expected; its high ASE enrichment and distinctive HNF4A interaction structure were the biologically informative findings. Combined Annotation Dependent Depletion (CADD) analyses further supported a stronger relationship between HNF4A-related predictions and predicted deleteriousness in this cluster. CONCLUSIONS: Integration of single-nucleus chromatin accessibility data with an interpretable XGBoost-SHAP framework provides a method for prioritizing noncoding variants and identifying nonlinear regulatory relationships in a specific developmental context. Within this framework, the stronger relationship between HNF4A-related predictions and CADD-predicted deleteriousness in the lower-MAF cluster is consistent with selective constraint on HNF4A-bound regulatory elements and suggests a hypothesis for how lower-frequency noncoding variation may contribute to intrafamilial phenotypic variability in HNF4A-related Maturity-Onset Diabetes of the Young (MODY1).

works.title: VENAS2: Bidirectional Mutation Modeling for Genomic Surveillance Reveals Reversions and Hidden Transmission Links in Pathogens
works.abstract: Accurately resolving pathogen evolution is essential for genomic surveillance, yet existing approaches often assume unidirectional mutation accumulation and fail to capture reversions that obscure lineage classification and transmission dynamics. Here we present VENAS2, a scalable framework that integrates genomic, temporal and geographic information to construct spatiotemporal evolutionary networks while explicitly modeling bidirectional mutational processes. Applied to 7.25 million SARS-CoV-2 genomes from GISAID between December 2019 and June 2024, VENAS2 reconstructed the evolutionary history of SARS-CoV-2 and precisely inferred the temporal dynamics of major variants of concern. Further application to the Viridian dataset revealed 4,654 distinct genomic sites with at least one potential reversion event, providing a systematic view of potential reversion signals during viral evolution. Extending to Mycobacterium tuberculosis, VENAS2 delineated major lineages and identified over threefold additional transmission clusters beyond conventional genomic distance-based methods, uncovering hidden links enriched for drug-resistant strains. These results demonstrate VENAS2's capacity to uncover cryptic evolutionary processes across viruses and bacteria, providing a generalizable platform that bridges genomic surveillance with actionable public health response.

works.title: NLP-12/Cholecystokinin signaling stabilizes sensory dendritic structure and protects neuronal healthspan in Caenorhabditis elegans
works.abstract: Aging selectively degrades neuronal structure and function, yet the signals that actively preserve neuronal integrity over adult life remain incompletely defined. In Caenorhabditis elegans, the PVD sensory neuron develops progressive excessive higher-order dendritic branching during normal aging that correlates with declines in proprioceptive locomotion. Using this system as a quantitative in vivo readout of neuronal healthspan, we identify the cholecystokinin-like neuropeptide NLP-12 as a protective signal that preserves PVD homeostasis across adulthood. nlp-12 loss-of-function animals show early-onset excessive branching and earlier declines in proprioceptive function, whereas nlp-12 overexpression attenuates excessive branching in aged adults without extending lifespan, indicating a neuron-focused effect on healthspan. Longitudinal analysis of an NLP-12::mKate reporter reveals age-related reduction in extracellular delivery of NLP-12 and increased retention in the soma of the DVA interneuron, where nlp-12 is predominantly expressed. Consistent with a requirement for secretory trafficking, disrupting the NLP-12 signal peptide abolishes the rescue effects of wild-type nlp-12 reintroduction in nlp-12 mutants. Additionally, chemogenetic silencing of DVA during adulthood similarly accelerates excessive PVD branching, supporting an ongoing requirement for secreted DVA-derived NLP-12. Receptor genetics further show that both cholecystokinin receptor homologs, CKR-1 and CKR-2, are required downstream of NLP-12-mediated neuroprotection during aging. Finally, human cholecystokinin rescues PVD branching and partially improves proprioceptive patterning in nlp-12 mutants, supporting functional conservation. Together, these findings define conserved cholecystokinin-like neuropeptide signaling as an adult maintenance mechanism that buffers age-associated decline in neuronal resilience.

works.title: Holistic integration of protein interaction datasets establishes a framework for exploring the organization and composition of Caenorhabditis elegans germ granules
works.abstract: Spatiotemporal organization of biological molecules is a key driver of cellular processes, including many post-transcriptional epigenetic processes. The germline-specific germ granules are biomolecular condensates that act as hubs for mRNA and small RNA processing and are core regulators of germline gene expression programming. Germ granules have been studied extensively in Caenorhabditis elegans, and recent developments have led to many subdivisions of the germ granule into specialized compartments. Rapid advancements in microscopy and protein-protein interaction (PPI) screening techniques have produced a large amount of data towards characterizing the localization of proteins to specific granules. However, common methods used to probe PPIs are limited in their ability to robustly detect valid interactions, especially the multivalent and sometimes transient ones observed in granule environments. Here we perform a meta-analysis of granule protein interaction screens. While these experiments generally enrich for proteins matching the profile of granule-associated proteins, we find that when considering screens individually, reproducibility is surprisingly low, highlighting not only the variability inherent in these methods but also the dynamic nature of the PPI networks present in granules. We developed an algorithm to provide a measure of each protein's association with specific granules across various experiments (a "granule association metric" or GAM). By further clustering and investigation of the GAM matrix, we demonstrate the power of this holistic approach to provide deeper insights into germ granule organization, highlight novel candidates, and act as a resource to inform future investigations into granules and their constituent proteins.

works.title: Differential selection between sexes and the evolution of recombination in haplodiploids
works.abstract: Eusocial Hymenoptera present the highest known recombination rates among metazoans, which evolved several times independently among bees, ants and wasps. Several hypotheses have been proposed to explain this observation, including stronger selection for recombination caused by coevolving parasites and pathogens, and strong sexual selection among haploid males due to male-biased sex ratios among reproductive individuals. In this article, we explore the effects of haplodiploidy and differential selection between sexes on the evolution of recombination, by analyzing a three-locus model in which selection for recombination stems from negative epistasis between selected loci. Our analytical predictions are compared with the results of individual-based simulations in which deleterious mutations occur along a linear chromosome. Our results show that, at mutation-selection balance for deleterious alleles, increasing the strength of selection against deleterious alleles (due to the effect of male haploidy and/or sexual selection) tends to reduce selection for recombination. However, an increase in the overall magnitude of negative epistasis (which may also be due to male haploidy and/or sexual selection) combined with the fact that recombination only occurs in females may increase selection for recombination substantially. Our model also shows that, in conditions favoring recombination, increasing recombination in meioses leading to parthenogenetic ovules (and male offspring) may yield stronger benefits than in meioses leading to fertilized ovules (and female offspring).

works.title: Spatial relief of Kinesin-1 auto-inhibition by Ensconsin regulates ncMTOCs localization and shapes microtubule networks
works.abstract: During Drosophila oogenesis, the organization of microtubules (MTs) drives polarized transport and cytoplasmic flows. Although Kinesin-1 plays a central role in these processes, its molecular and spatial regulation remains poorly understood. Here, we show that Ensconsin, an activator of the Kinesin heavy chain (Khc), is enriched in the oocyte through MT binding, Dynein-mediated transport and by the MT-anchoring protein Ninein. Strikingly, loss of Ensconsin enrichment reduces cortical non-centrosomal microtubule-organizing centers (ncMTOCs), weakens MT nucleation, impairs MT organization and MT-dependent cytoplasmic flows. Additionally, a specific Khc variant unable to bind Ensconsin, is constitutively active and is able to partly rescue the loss of Ensconsin in oocyte and neural stem cells, thereby providing in vivo support for the relief-of-auto-inhibition model. Overall, we uncover a novel function for the Khc-Ensconsin complex in the recruitment of ncMTOCs in oocytes for MT organization. Our findings are in line with a model in which Ensconsin enrichment acts as a rheostat to modulate Khc activation, ensuring precise spatial remodeling of the microtubule cytoskeleton in the oocyte.

works.title: Remodeling of the olfactory mucosa: maturation of glia, fibroblasts and vascular compartments after birth
works.abstract: Despite extensive research on the olfactory epithelium during embryonic and postnatal stages, little is known about peripartum adaptations. Here we describe the profound changes that occur between E18 and P8 - shortly after birth and exposure to air. In the lamina propria, we observed a significant expansion of extracellular space and axon bundles. Olfactory ensheathing cells, the glia cells of the lamina propria, stopped proliferating and upregulate SOX10 after birth. In addition, only after birth did olfactory ensheathing cells express CLDN5 and PECAM1, both of which tighten blood vessels, as well as gap junction communication and potassium transport proteins. Functional Bowman glands emerged only after birth, similar as the layer of horizontal basal cells. Since horizontal basal cells produce extracellular matrix proteins, laminin localization changed after these cells populated the basal epithelium. Interestingly, embryonic mice showed multiple invaginations of blood vessels throughout the olfactory epithelium, which disappear immediately after birth. Our findings reveal that the lamina propria of the olfactory mucosa undergoes profound postnatal maturation, leading to the establishment of a specialized adult tissue architecture.

works.title: NFE2L1 promotes cisplatin resistance by attenuating ferroptosis through SLC27A2-mediated fatty acid metabolism in ovarian cancer
works.abstract: Approaches that promote ferroptosis have emerged as promising therapeutic strategies for chemotherapy-resistant cancers; however, the mechanisms regulating ferroptosis during acquired therapeutic resistance remain incompletely understood. Using RNA sequencing, we identified that Nuclear Factor Erythroid-2 Related Factor 1 (NFE2L1) is upregulated in cisplatin-resistant ovarian cancer (OC) cells and patient tissues, as well as in ferroptosis-resistant models. Genetic knockdown of NFE2L1 resensitized cells to cisplatin both in vitro and in vivo. Notably, this effect was largely reversed by ferroptosis inhibitors, which significantly rescued cell survival following NFE2L1 depletion under cisplatin treatment. Further experiments demonstrated that modulating NFE2L1 expression affects the response to ferroptosis inducers by regulating iron accumulation and lipid peroxidation. Mechanistically, NFE2L1 silencing increased the transcription of long-chain fatty acid transport protein 2 (SLC27A2/FATP2). Chromatin immunoprecipitation and dual-luciferase reporter assays showed that NFE2L1 bound directly to the SLC27A2 promoter, where it competitively inhibited the recruitment of the transcription factor SP1. As a key member of the long-chain acyl-CoA synthetase family, FATP2 promotes the uptake and activation of long-chain fatty acids, processes that have been implicated in the regulation of ferroptosis. Subsequent LC-MS-based lipidomic analysis revealed that NFE2L1 reprogrammed intracellular fatty acid metabolism, characterized by increased polyunsaturated fatty acid (PUFA) levels and decreased monounsaturated fatty acid (MUFA) levels within phosphatidylethanolamines (PEs), thereby increasing cellular susceptibility to ferroptosis. Consistent with these findings, supplementation with exogenous unsaturated fatty acids modulated NFE2L1-mediated ferroptosis sensitivity. Collectively, our findings reveal a novel NFE2L1/SLC27A2 axis that drives cisplatin resistance in OC by suppressing ferroptosis, and suggest a potential therapeutic strategy for treating cisplatin-resistant ovarian cancer.

works.title: Progress and disparities in fungal genomics in the long-read era
A framework for genome-wide characterization of DNA methylation and variant effect prediction
works.abstract: DNA methylation plays a critical role in many essential biological processes, including transcriptional regulation, genomic imprinting, chromosomal maintenance, genomic stability and development, and has phenotypic and disease impacts. However, genome-wide characterization of methylation patterns across cell types and tissues remains a major challenge. Here, to address this, we present a framework that enables systematic genome-wide analysis of methylation and sequence-based prediction of context-specific methylation effects of variants. Our data-driven discovery of methylation classes reveals context-dependent roles for methylation across tissues, cell types and regions of the genome. The framework also includes Wreath, a deep learning-based sequence model specifically designed to accurately predict the context-dependent impact of any genetic variant on methylation. These developments leverage a compendium that harmonizes disparate methylation profiles from disparate studies including over 90 tissues and cell types. Using Wreath, we systematically characterized the impact of noncoding pathogenic variants on tissue-specific methylation, generating mechanistic hypotheses for individual regulatory variants. We make the full framework, including the compendium, the methylation classes and the model, available for use by the community. This study introduces a framework for integrating DNA methylation data across more than 90 tissues and cell types, characterizing genome-wide methylation patterns and predicting context-specific effects of genetic variants on DNA methylation and regulatory function using a deep learning model, Wreath.

works.title: Hematotoxicity: the hidden legacy of CAR T cell therapy
AI-based precision prognostics and therapy personalization for childhood brain tumors
works.abstract: Accurate prediction of patient outcomes remains a critical challenge in oncology, in particular for childhood brain tumors, in which treatment decisions need to carefully balance risk of tumor recurrence and death against severe therapy-induced sequelae. Here, we developed MANTIS (methylation profiling and artificial neural networks for time-dependent individualized survival predictions), a precision artificial intelligence (AI) tool for medulloblastoma and ependymoma outcome prediction built on genome-wide DNA methylation array data from 2,786 patients. MANTIS generates individualized survival probabilities over a 10-year period and achieves concordance indices as high as 0.80 ± 0.07, significantly exceeding the predictive accuracy of current clinical indicators. Extending MANTIS to estimate individualized treatment effects identifies ~60% of patients with average-risk medulloblastoma without a significant survival disadvantage (P = 0.683) when treated with less intensive craniospinal irradiation doses, which is associated with improved neurocognitive outcomes. In conclusion, our study establishes a foundation for AI-based precision prognostics and therapy personalization in childhood brain tumors and offers a blueprint for similar initiatives in other cancer types.

works.title: Distinct DAXX effector modules separate H3.3 nucleosome assembly from ERV repression
works.abstract: Endogenous retroviruses (ERVs) can compromise genome integrity when expressed, and cells have evolved chromatin-based pathways to repress their transcription. The histone H3.3 chaperone DAXX localizes to a subset of ERVs embedded in KAP1-SETDB1-associated heterochromatin and contributes to their repression. Here, we define distinct DAXX determinants that support H3.3 deposition versus ERV repression. Using complementary biochemical and genetic approaches, we identify a conserved basic patch within the DAXX histone-binding domain that engages DNA, promotes H3.3 nucleosome assembly in vitro, and is required for H3.3 enrichment at DAXX-bound ERVs in cells. Despite failure to deposit H3.3, DAXX with substitutions in this basic patch retains localization to ERVs and preserves repression, indicating that H3.3 deposition is dispensable for DAXX-dependent ERV repression. In contrast, disruption of the DAXX C-terminal SUMO-interacting motif impairs DAXX-dependent ERV repression and SUMO-dependent effector engagement, including MORC3 recruitment. These findings define separable outputs downstream from DAXX recruitment, uncoupling nucleosome assembly from ERV repression and placing SUMO-dependent effector engagement within the broader KAP1-SETDB1-centered ERV repression network.

works.title: EnzyREx: deep learning enables reaction-based comprehensive enzyme screening
works.abstract: Orphan enzymes for which the corresponding genes remain unidentified represent a major gap in functional annotation in genomic analysis. We present EnzyREx, an AI-based framework for comprehensive enzyme screening, to explore novel enzyme candidates. EnzyREx consists of two deep learning models to classify proteins as enzymes and non-enzymes and predict catalytic capability for enzyme‒reaction pairs. Both models achieved performance comparable to or better than that of existing software. When applied to 1,255 microbiome-related orphan reactions, EnzyREx identified candidate proteins for 897 reactions. EnzyREx provides a scalable approach for linking unannotated proteins to orphan reactions and extending functional annotation.

works.title: UniqSketch: sensitive and resource-efficient strain-level detection in metagenomes
works.abstract: Microbial communities contain diverse organisms, including multiple coexisting strains of the same species that display phenotypic differences influencing pathogenicity and host interactions. Detecting strains is challenging because of computational demands and their low abundance in metagenomes. We present UniqSketch, an open-source toolkit for identifying target strains across species within a single metagenome. It tracks specific microbial signatures or contaminants even in complex, multi-species samples. UniqSketch uses unique genomic fingerprints and a compact Bloom filter for efficient computation and accurate abundance estimation. Results show improved precision and accuracy over existing tools, with reliable performance at sequencing coverage as low as 0.1×.

works.title: PhenX Toolkit: a knowledgebase that enables consistent data collection and facilitates cross-study analysis and data reuse
works.abstract: The PhenX (consensus measures for Phenotypes and eXposures) Toolkit (https://www.phenxtoolkit.org/) is a publicly available knowledgebase of well-established, broadly validated measurement protocols recommended for use in genomic, clinical, translational, and epidemiological research involving human participants. Consistent use of PhenX protocols, including questionnaires, bioassays, and physical assessments, improves the rigor, transparency, reproducibility, and comparability of research data. The Toolkit was recently highlighted in the National Institutes of Health (NIH) implementation plan, "Leading in Gold Standard Science," as an example of efforts to advance reproducible biomedical research. The Toolkit currently includes 1010 protocols spanning a wide range of diseases, exposures, and study designs. Content development is guided by the scientific community through a consensus-based process involving expert Working Groups, community input, and strategic oversight from the PhenX Steering Committee. Collaborations with NIH Institutes have expanded Toolkit content in priority areas, including substance use and cardiovascular disease. The PhenX Toolkit enhances study design and supports implementation of selected protocols. PhenX also collaborates with resources that facilitate data collection (REDCap), data standards (LOINC), and data repositories to promote interoperability and cross-study analyses. To date, the Toolkit has been recommended in 711 NIH funding opportunities and cited in >1300 publications. Future directions are discussed.

works.title: Whole-proteome structure/function prediction in uropathogenic E. coli reveals previously missed host-microbe and microbe-phage interaction pathways
works.abstract: The rapid advancement of high-throughput sequencing technologies has vastly increased the number of known protein sequences, but the experimental characterization of their structures and functions lags behind. This gap in knowledge impedes our understanding of biological mechanisms of these proteins, hinders the interpretation of high-throughput experiments, and exposes a significant challenge in modern biology: deducing the structural and functional information of proteins based on their sequences. Most computational approaches rely on homology with well-annotated proteins, yet many proteins lack identifiable homologues, reducing the power of this approach. Here, we integrated cutting-edge protein structure and function prediction methods to develop a complete sequence-structure-function pipeline that predicts structures and functions based on primary sequences. We applied this pipeline to predict the structure and function of all proteins in Escherichia coli UTI89, a model strain of uropathogenic E. coli. Based on the predicted functions, we performed enrichment analysis on the whole genome and revealed the possible roles and related biological mechanisms of poorly annotated proteins in this organism. Moreover, the performance of our pipeline was further validated through detailed case studies of the UTI89_C0931 and ybtS genes. Finally, we compiled the UTI89 structure and function database (https://seq2fun.dcmb.med.umich.edu/UTI89), offering it as a crucial resource to aid researchers in elucidating the roles of unannotated proteins. This database aims to bridge critical knowledge gaps in microbial pathogenicity and resistance, enhancing our capacity to tackle emerging health threats.

works.title: Leaving X: How scale insects repeatedly evolved alternatives to chromosomal sex determination
works.abstract: Abstract Reproduction is a core feature of life, yet it is still unclear why sex determination systems are conserved for hundreds of millions of years in some taxa but repeatedly turn over in others. A prime example is the true bugs; the vast majority of families employ a conserved X sex chromosomal system, but in scale insects (Coccomorpha), sex determination systems are more varied. Scale insects may retain X chromosomes, employ a form of haplodiploidy known as paternal genome elimination (PGE), or reproduce via selfing as simultaneous hermaphrodites. We sequenced 17 new scale insect species to study sex determination transitions. We recovered two independent losses of the X, once in the family Monophlebidae and a second time at the base of the PGE families. In the former, genomic rearrangements begin before the X is lost, leading to a pair of massive autosomes to which the X fuses in hermaphrodites. In the latter, the X chromosome has multiple fates, from being preserved intact, albeit without sex determination function, to being reshuffled as part of a massive whole genome rearrangement in mealybugs. We analyzed ortholog conservation across the transitions and found few genes lost, with only one orthogroup lost in both, and a number of orthogroups gained, suggesting these transitions did not require large changes to gene content. Finally, extreme sexual dimorphism of gene expression predates sex determination turnover and lingers on some formerly X-linked sequences. Together, these results illustrate the multiple routes to sex determination turnover, refine causal hypotheses, and provide a wealth of new resources for genomic study of scale insects.

works.title: Maternal genomic legacy of Altaic-speaking populations reveals broad Eurasian maternal lineage diversity with a northern East Asian connection
works.abstract: Mitochondrial DNA (mtDNA), inherited maternally and without recombination, is crucial for tracing maternal lineages and studying population history. Although Altaic-speaking groups are widespread across Eurasia, their maternal genetic data remain limited. Here, we assembled a comparative dataset of 58,257 modern and 7,425 ancient individuals, including high-quality mtDNA single-nucleotide polymorphism variation data from large-scale array studies of representative Altaic individuals. This dataset enabled a detailed assessment of maternal genetic diversity and geographic structure in Altaic-speaking populations. Our results reveal diverse patterns of maternal haplogroup composition among Altaic-speaking populations, including lineages whose distributions align with enrichment in ancient mtDNA datasets from archaeological contexts associated with subsistence strategies such as hunter-gathering, pastoralism, and farming across northern East Asia, Siberia, and western Eurasia. Manchu and Mongolian populations show stronger maternal affinity with northern East Asians, whereas Kazakhs carry higher proportions of western and northern Eurasian lineages. Manchu populations show some north-south differentiation across different geographic grouping schemes. This study expands mtDNA resources for underrepresented Altaic-speaking populations and improves understanding of their maternal genetic diversity.

works.title: On the limits of detection of higher-order epistatic interactions
works.abstract: The function of microbial communities is often dominated by additive and pairwise interactions, raising the question of whether this reflects intrinsic biological simplicity or fundamental limits of detection. Here, we leverage the theory of fitness landscapes to bridge microbial ecology and genetics, and show that this apparent simplicity is a generic consequence of structural and statistical constraints rather than evidence for intrinsically weak higher-order interactions. We separate the detectability of individual epistatic interactions from their contribution to functional variance, and demonstrate that local k-order interactions suffer from exponential noise amplification while their contributions to total variance are intrinsically suppressed by order-dependent geometric dilution arising from the combinatorial structure of the landscape. Applying this framework to a fully sampled 210 experimental microbial landscape, we find that only first- and second-order interactions are distinguishable from experimental noise. Furthermore, generalized Lotka-Volterra landscapes reveal that experimental noise alone can generate the illusion of higher-order structure in communities where all direct mechanistic interactions are pairwise and indirect interactions are weak. Our findings identify universal, order-dependent limits on the quantification of epistasis that apply to high-dimensional landscapes across ecology and genetics, providing a principled foundation for rational community design.

works.title: Correction to: The deacetylase Sir2 is the primary sensor driving transcriptional changes in response to low NAD+ in the yeast Kluyveromyces lactis
Targeting the circ_0042819-PLA2G6 axis sensitizes multiple myeloma to proteasome inhibitors through ferroptosis induction
works.abstract: Multiple myeloma (MM) is a refractory plasma cell neoplasm characterized by frequent development of drug resistance, leading to poor clinical outcomes. Activation of ferroptosis, an iron-dependent form of cell death driven by lipid peroxidation, has emerged as a promising cancer therapeutic strategy. In this study, we show that the circular RNA circ_0042819 exhibits high expression in both bone marrow and plasma samples from MM patients, with its overexpression strongly associated with disease progression and unfavorable prognosis. Mechanistically, circ_0042819 directly interacts with Up-frameshift protein 1 (UPF1) in MM cells, and the circ_0042819-UPF1 complex upregulates the expression of phospholipase A2 group VI (PLA2G6) via interacting with, and thus stabilizing, its mRNA. Furthermore, the circ_0042819-PLA2G6 axis suppresses ferroptosis through phospholipid remodeling in MM cells. Importantly, depletion of circ_0042819 or PLA2G6 enhances MM sensitivity to proteasome inhibitors (bortezomib and carfilzomib) by promoting ferroptosis both in vitro and in vivo. Collectively, our findings demonstrate that circ_0042819 is a potential non-invasive biomarker for the diagnosis and prognosis of MM, and that inhibition of the circ_0042819-PLA2G6 axis can mitigate the resistance of MM to proteasome inhibitors through ferroptosis sensitization, thus suggesting a novel therapeutic approach.

works.title: Clonal hematopoiesis and cytopenias following CAR19 therapy
works.abstract: CD19-directed chimeric antigen receptor T cell therapy (CAR19) improves survival in relapsed/refractory large B cell lymphoma compared with immunochemotherapy with intent for autologous hematopoietic cell transplantation (autoHCT). However, major toxicities include prolonged cytopenias, infection and secondary hematologic malignancies. Here, to investigate these complications, we studied patients with lymphoma receiving CAR19 and compared clinical outcomes to propensity-matched autoHCT-treated controls. CAR19-treated patients exhibited impaired immune reconstitution and increased infection. Bone marrow analysis showed that prolonged post-CAR cytopenias are associated with clonal cytopenias of undetermined significance and interferon-mediated inflammation. Clonal hematopoiesis (CH) commonly expanded following CAR19 infusion and was associated with impaired immune reconstitution and treatment-related myeloid malignancy (tMN). Post-CAR tMN was molecularly and clinically comparable to post-autoHCT tMN. Single-cell DNA analysis revealed mostly independent CH clones, while CAR integration into CH-mutant T cells occurred frequently and may drive expansion and persistence. Together, these findings implicate CH expansion and marrow inflammation in key CAR19-associated toxicities. This study shows that clonal hematopoiesis expands after chimeric antigen receptor (CAR) T cell therapy and contributes to secondary myeloid cancers. In addition, the CAR vector frequently integrates into pre-existing clonal hematopoiesis.

works.title: A catalog of transcriptome genetic regulation in a consanguineous Middle Eastern biobank
works.abstract: Ancestry-specific genetic mapping of transcriptome regulation is pivotal for understanding genome function, especially in underrepresented consanguineous populations. Here we characterized 1,882 Qatar Biobank participants, integrating blood RNA sequencing, whole-genome sequencing and phenotypic data across 45 clinically relevant traits. We cataloged ~7 million significant quantitative trait loci (QTLs), both short and structural variants, impacting gene expression, isoform usage, splicing and allele-specific expression, uncovering 1,379 novel eGenes. Fine-mapping resolved 29,953 high-confidence, independent causal loci including 24% previously unreported as well as those with effect alleles showing significant divergence across global populations, while 1,371 were absent from public databases. Leveraging elevated autozygosity, we found that causal variants are depleted from runs of homozygosity, consistent with purifying selection, while recent autozygosity increased the burden of homozygous regulatory variants. We identified QTLs with recessive deleterious effects on 10 Mendelian disease genes and homozygous QTLs causing extreme outlier expression in 66 genes including dosage-sensitive ones. Colocalization analysis revealed 58 causal variants acting on 20 clinically relevant phenotypes, implicating novel genes including ATP6V0B and RQCD1 in metabolic and blood disorders. These findings establish this QTL catalog as a valuable Middle Eastern resource for genome interpretation and genomic medicine.
