We develop a targeted amplicon-based panel including 979 markers (845 autosomal and 80 X Chromosome DNPs, plus 54 Y SNPs), and test at depths ranging from 1,000× to 10,000× on 42 individuals, including genomic DNA from 4 families, 2 artificial maternal-child mixtures simulating cfDNA and actual cfDNA from 12 pregnant women plus the putative biological fathers. We observe a DNP sequencing error rate of 8.9×10 -5 , i.e. ~12 times lower than the observed single base error rate. By exploiting the full range of sequencing depths at loci supporting the fetal genotype, we obtain Combined Paternity Index curves that consistently lead to the correct paternity attribution or exclusion in all true or false mother-father pairs. Notably, NEWPAT proves effective even at fetal cfDNA levels as low as 0.2%, when existing SNP-based protocols lead to inconclusive results, offering a highly sensitive and accurate NIPAT strategy.

works.title: Developmental transcriptomic analysis of primary mouse cortical neurons reveals sex-specific expression of neuropeptides
works.abstract: Primary neuronal cultures derived from mouse tissue serve as an essential model for investigating neuronal development and function. Despite this, comprehensive developmental and sex-specific transcriptomic profiles in primary neurons have not been defined. Here, we perform multiplexed RNA sequencing of neurons derived from male and female cortices across time. We validate this approach by assessing established neuronal maturation genes and identify highly stable genes to serve as controls across development. Next, using linear modeling and temporal regression, we define developmentally regulated transcripts, longitudinal expression dynamics, and gene signatures associated with transition states throughout development. Unexpectedly, this also reveals sex-specific effects on autosomal genes that emerge only after neuronal maturation even in the absence of in vivo cues. Most notably, neuropeptide genes Cortistatin and Neurokinin A are more highly expressed in female neurons. Furthermore, exposure to these neuropeptides elicits distinct transcriptional responses in male- versus female-derived cultures. These findings provide a valuable resource and reveal sex-specific autosomal transcriptional signatures that emerge in neurons maintained ex vivo.

works.title: Revisiting the concept of mitotic DNA synthesis: is it a mitosis-driven reaction?
works.abstract: More than a decade ago, a novel DNA repair pathway termed mitotic DNA synthesis (MiDAS) was proposed to complete DNA replication during early mitosis and minimise chromosome missegregation. This proposal was based on unscheduled incorporation of 5-ethynyl-2′-deoxyuridine (EdU) at common fragile sites (CFSs) in mitotic cells that experienced mild replication stress, together with the involvement of proteins implicated in break-induced replication (BIR). Since then, increasing attention has focused on the mechanisms underlying MiDAS. However, the widely adopted MiDAS assay has several fundamental limitations and cannot conclusively demonstrate de novo DNA synthesis initiated during mitosis. In this Comment, I discuss these limitations and clarify the conceptual distinction between the phenomenon of DNA synthesis in mitosis and MiDAS DNA repair. I propose alternative explanations and urge caution in attributing MiDAS solely to mitotic BIR without rigorously considering other possibilities, including the continuation of DNA replication across the G2-M transition and BIR initiated in G2 that persists into mitosis. These considerations highlight the need for experimental approaches capable of distinguishing newly initiated mitotic DNA synthesis from pre-existing DNA synthesis/repair. This Comment urges caution in attributing MiDAS solely to mitotic BIR, encouraging the use of approaches capable of distinguishing newly initiated mitotic DNA synthesis from pre-existing replication.

works.title: Differential roles for the spindle assembly checkpoint in error surveillance and mitotic timing
works.abstract: Spindle assembly checkpoint (SAC) components have been proposed to act as both a surveillance mechanism monitoring mitotic fidelity and as a timer that ensures sufficient time for chromosome alignment to occur. To evaluate these roles, we utilized an SAC-deficient cell line generated by eliminating the full-length Cdc20 translational isoform (Cdc20 ∆FL), and defined genetic interactions using CRISPR/Cas9-based screening. Cdc20 ∆FL cells display synthetic-lethal relationships with genes required for chromosome segregation, highlighting the role of the SAC in error surveillance. Interestingly, we found that the SAC component Mad2, which has been proposed to act as an essential "timer" to control anaphase onset by preventing premature APC/C activation, becomes dispensable for viability in Cdc20 ∆FL cells. Our targeted analysis indicates that regulation of mitotic timing involves a combination of Mad2 inhibition of APC/C-Cdc20, Cdk1-mediated Cdc20 phosphorylation preventing premature APC/C-Cdc20 activation, and total Cdc20 protein levels. Simultaneously perturbing these pathways results in premature mitotic exit and catastrophic chromosome mis-segregation.

works.title: OBITUARY: Ada Yonath (1939–2026): Pioneering the Quest for the Ribosome Structure
Midzone bundles of the mammalian anaphase spindle are mechanically coupled both locally and globally
works.abstract: Robust chromosome segregation requires the anaphase spindle to both preserve and remodel its structure under force. How it does so remains unclear as probing mechanics during anaphase’s short lifetime is challenging. Here, we use microneedles to pull on mammalian anaphase midzone bundles and ask how they respond to and transmit force across space and time. We find that midzone bundles locally transmit force to each other in the spindle’s short axis over multiple timescales. Along the spindle’s long axis, midzone bundles globally transmit force: rather than bundles sliding apart or detaching under force, the spindle shortens. This reveals strong anchorage and resistance to outward sliding, and that spindle elongation requires all midzone bundles to elongate. This global force transmission is stronger for short-lived forces and is strictly PRC1-dependent, indicating limited mechanistic redundancy. In sum, the anaphase spindle acts as a single mechanical unit over short timescales to resist and transmit force, while remodeling over long timescales to segregate chromosomes.

works.title: Adhesion integrity activates mechanosensitive proliferative signaling
works.abstract: Weakening of adherens junctions (AJs) and focal adhesions (FAs) adhesiveness has been proposed to enable cancer initiation and progression. Here we report that E-cadherin at cell–cell contacts and vinculin at FAs are transiently under higher tension in MCF10A cells overactivating the Src proto-oncogene. Knockdown of paxillin or P-cadherin, or inhibition of focal adhesion kinase (FAK) or AJ assembly with EGTA, suppresses this force increase across both E-cadherin and vinculin. FAK and P-cadherin trans-homophilic interactions further enhance Src-dependent myosin II and extracellular signal-regulated kinase (ERK) activation. In addition, FAK and P-cadherin potentiate ERK and serum response factor (SRF) signaling, thereby supporting cell proliferation. Furthermore, knockdown of Drosophila cadherin or alpha integrin suppresses Src-induced tissue overgrowth, reinforcing the role of adhesion integrity in Src-driven proliferation. Thus, prior to the loss of cell–cell and cell–matrix adhesiveness, adhesion integrity by P-cadherin at AJs and FAK at FAs could represent a critical step enabling premalignant cells to gain a proliferative advantage.

works.title: Epithelial-to-mesenchymal transition confers mechanical resistance to hemodynamic stress during hematogenous dissemination
works.abstract: Metastatic dissemination requires circulating tumor cells (CTCs) to survive hemodynamic forces, yet the biological traits that enable survival under fluid shear stress (FSS) remain poorly defined. While current paradigms suggest that fluid shear stress (FSS) broadly induces an epithelial-to-mesenchymal transition (EMT), we investigated an alternative mechanism: FSS acts as a mechanical bottleneck that selectively enriches for pre-existing mesenchymal cancer cells by destroying more epithelial-like phenotypes prior to detectable changes in EMT marker expression. Using epithelial and mesenchymal subpopulations isolated from the same cell lines, we exposed single cells in suspension to pulsatile FSS to demonstrate that mesenchymal cells exhibit significantly higher survival rates and lower membrane rupture following pulsatile FSS. Immediate post-shear single-cell analysis revealed stable vimentin-to-cytokeratin (VIM/KRT) ratios in mesenchymal populations, whereas epithelial-like populations showed a selective loss of low-VIM/KRT cells, consistent with immediate mechanical depletion prior to biological induction of EMT. Direct manipulation of EMT states confirmed this causal relationship: TGFβ-induced EMT rescued survival in epithelial cells, while E-cadherin overexpression sensitized mesenchymal cells to mechanical rupture. To validate these findings clinically, we analyzed single-cell RNA-seq data from three patient-derived CTC datasets and found that higher VIM/KRT ratios significantly correlate with increased CTC abundance in the bloodstream. Together, these results demonstrate that hemodynamic forces impose a deterministic mechanical selection pressure on CTCs, identifying epithelial-associated biophysical traits as a primary therapeutic vulnerability in the metastatic cascade.

works.title: HMGB1 directly activates BAP1 transcription to sustain tumor growth in mesothelioma
works.abstract: BAP1 and HMGB1 alterations are implicated in the pathogenesis of mesothelioma, an aggressive cancer of the membranes covering the thoracic and abdominal cavities. Genetic inactivating mutations of BAP1 cause cancer in ~100% of carriers. The mechanism/s that regulate BAP1 expression were unknown. We discovered that HMGB1 directly modulates BAP1 expression. Studying our Hmgb1 knock-out mouse mesothelioma models, primary fibroblasts obtained from carriers of pathogenic heterozygous germline BAP1 mutations, and mesothelioma cell lines, we discovered that HMGB1 loss caused a significant reduction in BAP1 expression and protein levels, whereas HMGB1 overexpression increased BAP1 mRNA and protein levels. We demonstrated that HMGB1 binds to the BAP1 promoter and activates its transcription, leading to BAP1 overexpression, which in turn promoted the proliferation, migration, and invasion of mesothelioma cells. These findings were confirmed in lung, colon, and cholangiocarcinoma cell lines. These findings indicate that while BAP1 inactivating mutations promote cancer development, cancer cells that do not express BAP1 are less aggressive, pointing to the HMGB1-BAP1 axis as a novel attractive target for therapy. Furthermore, our discovery that HMGB1-driven BAP1 overexpression supports cancer growth provides a mechanistic rationale for the improved survival observed in mesothelioma patients with somatic BAP1 inactivating mutations.

works.title: Fhl2 promotes chondrocyte ferroptosis in osteoarthritis by impairing mitophagic flux through microtubule disorganization
Near-complete assembly of wild emmer wheat unveils centromere reorganization during polyploid evolution
High false sign rates in transcriptome-wide association studies
works.abstract: Abstract Transcriptome-wide association studies (TWAS) are widely used to identify genes involved in complex traits and to infer the direction of gene effects on traits. However, despite their popularity, it remains unclear how accurately TWAS recover the true direction of a gene’s effect on a trait. Here we estimate the false sign rate of TWAS for plasma proteins, leveraging the expectation that increased gene expression should generally increase protein expression. We then extend this framework to complex traits, where loss-of-function burden tests provide the expected direction of effect. In both analyses, we observe high discordance with expectations, with TWAS showing a false sign rate of 23% for plasma proteins and 33% for complex traits. We propose that much of the sign discordance arises when expression quantitative trait loci in non-trait-relevant tissues tag haplotypes associated with traits in genome-wide association studies via distinct, tightly linked regulatory variants, yielding spurious TWAS associations with the correct genes but with unreliable direction of effect. These findings show that TWAS-based direction-of-effect estimates should be interpreted with caution and raise concerns about the reliability of TWAS more broadly.

works.title: Co-regulation confounds direction of genetic effects in transcriptome-wide association studies
Molecular functions, cellular responses and pathological implications of the RNA modification N6-methyladenosine
HP1 can act independently of H3K9 methylation to promote heterochromatin focus formation, gene repression, and organogenesis
works.abstract: Histone post-translational modifications (PTMs) segregate genomes into heterochromatin and euchromatin by recruiting readers, such as Heterochromatin Protein 1, which binds methylation of histone H3 lysine 9 (H3K9me). Here, we report H3K9me-independent functions for the C. elegans HP1 orthologue HPL-2 and the H3K9 methyltransferase MET-2/SETDB1. The two colocalize in H3K9me-containing subnuclear foci independently of the PTM and each other. Their combined loss additively disrupts gene repression and organogenesis. A mutant HPL-2 deficient for H3K9me binding maintains localization to heterochromatin foci, restricts cell-fate decisions, and represses developmental genes, dependent on its multi-zinc-finger ligand, LIN-13. MET-2, catalytically active or not, requires its cofactor LIN-65 to form foci and silence genes in vivo. Molecular dynamics simulations and in vitro assays suggest that cofactor-driven condensate assemblies underlie H3K9me-independent focus formation in vivo, which correlates with gene silencing during organogenesis. This study defines two parallel, PTM-independent pathways through which a writer and reader can repress developmentally regulated genes.

works.title: The rapid delivery of RNase H variants reveals distinct classes of RNA:DNA hybrids
works.abstract: Multiple lines of evidence suggest that RNase H1-sensitive RNA:DNA hybrids could disrupt the stability and restart of stalled replication forks. The prolonged over-expression of RNase H1 is the most popular method to manipulate RNA:DNA hybrids in situ but it cannot discriminate between direct and indirect effects resulting from their loss. To overcome this limitation, we developed iCoRD (in Cellulo RNase H Delivery) to rapidly deliver comparable amounts of either Escherichia coli RNase H1 (RnhA) or control proteins in live cells, with a negligible impact on the transcriptome. iCoRD-delivered RnhA recognises RNA:DNA hybrids in situ, is enriched in the vicinity of active replication forks and rescues replication fork progression in different stress conditions. While iCoRD-delivered RnhA had a clear impact on stress-induced, fork-proximal RNA:DNA hybrids and R-ChIP signals, it had no effect on DRIP or S9.6 Cut&Tag signals, even when these were induced by stress. Our results strongly suggest the existence of distinct populations of RNA:DNA hybrids that are best mapped by different methods and are differently sensitive to RNase H1 activity in situ.

works.title: Multi-omics analysis of high-grade serous ovarian cancers reveals heterogeneity and distinct immunological patterns based upon clinico-genomic status
works.abstract: High-grade serous ovarian cancer (HGSOC) is characterized by remarkable intratumoral heterogeneity and variable tissue architectures, dictating differential therapeutic responses. Although BRCA1/2 mutations correlate with improved responses to DNA-damaging agents, how BRCA genotype shapes the tumor immune microenvironment (TIME) remains incompletely understood. Here, we integrated whole exome sequencing, total RNA sequencing and spatial transcriptomics to profile a cohort of BRCA-mutated (BRCA-MT) and non-BRCA-mutated (BRCA-WT) HGSOC tumors. While bulk transcriptomics highlighted global phenotypic shifts, suggesting a more pro-inflammatory milieu in BRCA-MT tumors, spatially resolved analysis revealed how these differences manifest within specific tissue architectures. Integrated clustering revealed recurrent spatial transcriptional states across genotypes. Specifically, we identified a transcriptionally distinct immune-enriched region (IC7) characterized by low tumor purity, interferon signaling, and antigen-presentation programs. Reference-based RCTD deconvolution provided orthogonal computational support that IC7 was enriched for T/NK and dendritic cells relative to non-IC7 regions. At the patient level, the functional state of IC7 was highly BRCA-dependent: BRCA-MT tumors exhibited stronger enrichment of interferon-α/γ responses and inflammatory signaling than BRCA-WT tumors. Exploratory CellChat analysis further suggested genotype-associated differences in predicted immune-related signaling. We also identify a conserved structural interface between CAF-like region (IC3) and macrophage-rich region (IC4), accompanied by a predicted CXCL12-CXCR4 chemokine recruitment axis. Taken together, these findings support a model in which BRCA mutation status is associated with functional differences within broadly conserved spatial regions, rather than extensive reorganization of the overall spatial architecture. This spatially resolved framework identifies BRCA-associated immune transcriptional patterns in HGSOC and provides a basis for future mechanistic validation.

works.title: A conserved motif in Pch2 regulates its localization and meiotic function in Saccharomyces cerevisiae
works.abstract: The Saccharomyces cerevisiae Pch2 protein is a conserved meiotic AAA+ ATPase whose activity must be tightly regulated to ensure proper chromosome dynamics during meiotic prophase I. Its function relies on remodeling the HORMA-domain protein Hop1, promoting conformational transitions that are essential for chromosome axis organization, checkpoint signaling, and recombination control. Here, we identify threonine 428 (T428), located within a conserved threonine-glutamine (TQ) motif, as a residue critical for Pch2 localization and function. We found that, in zip1Δ cells, the meiotic recombination checkpoint response is partially or completely abolished in the pch2-T428A and pch2-T428D mutants, respectively. Both mutations alter Pch2 subcellular localization, leading to its increased nuclear accumulation; however, forced nuclear exclusion of Pch2-T428A, but not Pch2-T428D, restores the zip1Δ meiotic block, indicating an additional effect of the T428D substitution on checkpoint function beyond subcellular distribution. Analysis in synapsis-proficient strains reveals that this residue also plays a critical role in coordinating Hop1 chromosomal enrichment with Mek1 activation along the synaptonemal complex. In contrast to pch2Δ or the ATPase-defective pch2-E399Q mutant, introduction of a negative charge at position 428 uncouples Hop1 accumulation from its phosphorylation, preventing Mek1 activation despite robust Hop1 association with meiotic chromosomes. These findings support emerging models in which Pch2 regulates Hop1 to control not only its chromosomal abundance, but also the maintenance of sufficient levels of Hop1 in a phosphorylation-competent conformation, thereby ensuring proper checkpoint signaling and faithful meiotic progression.

works.title: A high-throughput assay quantifies thermal scaling of Drosophila development with minute-scale precision
works.abstract: Precise regulation of developmental timing is essential for coordinated growth and robust development, yet staging remains technically challenging in many model systems. In Drosophila melanogaster, developmental timing has traditionally been assessed using low-throughput or coarse staging methods, limiting insight into how individual larval stages respond to environmental and genetic perturbations. Here, we present a high-throughput, real-time luminometry assay that enables continuous, automated measurement of postembryonic development in individual Drosophila larvae. By monitoring feeding-dependent luciferase activity, this method reliably detects transitions between larval instars and molts of individual larvae with minute-scale temporal resolution. Using this platform, we provide a quantitative, stage-resolved description of larval development across large cohorts, revealing distinct patterns of variability and weak temporal coupling between stages. We next examine how temperature shapes developmental timing across a broad thermal range. Increasing temperature uniformly accelerates larval development while preserving the proportional contribution of each stage, indicating that the temporal architecture of development is maintained as overall pace changes. Developmental rate follows predictable thermodynamic scaling within a defined temperature window, enabling precise estimation of thermal parameters at both whole-organism and stage-specific levels. Finally, we demonstrate that the assay is compatible with genetic perturbations and uncover a previously unrecognized intergenerational effect of parental temperature on offspring developmental timing. This work establishes a scalable, high-precision framework for measuring postembryonic development in Drosophila melanogaster. By revealing the modular and coordinated nature of larval growth, it enables systematic dissection of developmental timing and provides a platform to explore fundamental principles of developmental robustness across species.

works.title: A comprehensive HA-tagged PRC1 toolkit enables standardized chromatin profiling and proteomic analysis in Drosophila melanogaster
works.abstract: Polycomb group (PcG) proteins are evolutionarily conserved epigenetic regulators that maintain transcriptional states during development and are frequently dysregulated in disease. Here, we generated a comprehensive collection of endogenously HA-tagged alleles for the core components of Polycomb Repressive Complex 1 (PRC1) and additional chromatin regulators in Drosophila melanogaster using CRISPR/Cas9-mediated genome engineering. We show that endogenous HA tagging preserves protein expression, chromatin localization, and genome-wide binding profiles, enabling direct comparison using a common antibody to analyze distinct PcG subunits. Proteomic analyses recovered known components of canonical and non-canonical PRC1 and Polycomb Repressive Complex 2 (PRC2) complexes and identified additional PcG-associated factors. Notably, multiple components of the nuclear pore complex (NPC) were detected as PcG interactors, and genetic analyses confirmed a functional interaction between them. This resource provides a platform for standardized analysis of Polycomb function and chromatin regulation that can easily be extended to other chromatin regulatory complexes and applied across different developmental stages.

works.title: Breakdown of sporophytic self-incompatibility: diploids versus tetraploids
works.abstract: Many angiosperm species possess self-incompatibility (SI) systems that prevent self-fertilization. Because empirical studies often report higher selfing rates in tetraploids than in diploids, we investigate whether sporophytic self-incompatibility (SSI) is more likely to break down after the introduction of a self-compatible (SC) allele in tetraploid populations. To address this question, we use analytical models and individual-based simulations to compare diploid and tetraploid populations under two main scenarios: (1) all SI alleles are codominant, and (2) SI alleles are structured into dominance classes. Overall, our results indicate that SSI is more difficult to maintain in tetraploids than in diploids, with dominance relationships playing a key role in the invasion success of an SC allele. When SI alleles are organized into dominance classes, increasing the dominance of the SC allele generally favors SSI breakdown in tetraploids, while diploids show weaker sensitivity to dominance, with SSI maintained across all dominance scenarios for the SC allele under sufficiently high inbreeding depression. However, when the SC allele is dominant over all SI alleles, SSI is more readily maintained in both the codominant and dominance-class models.

works.title: GENETICS 2026 Reviewer Index
Substitutions in the yeast Nrd1 RNA-binding domain have distinct effects on NNS terminator recognition
works.abstract: RNA-binding proteins (RBPs) regulate gene expression through combinatorial interactions with RNAs and proteins. The essential S. cerevisiae nuclear RBP Nrd1 serves as a model to investigate the effects of RBPs on transcription and RNA processing. Nrd1 binding to short, noncoding RNAs elicits termination of their synthesis by RNA polymerase (RNAP) II, promotes polyadenylation by the TRAMP complex, and enables 3'-trimming by the nuclear exosome. How Nrd1 discriminates its substrate RNAs and coordinates these processes is not well understood. Here, we made deletions and substitutions in Nrd1 to assess the contributions of different domains to its function. We confirmed the contribution of known protein interaction domains in NNS terminator recognition and identified a region C-terminal to the RNA-binding domain (RBD) required for efficient termination in vivo. We also characterized three RBD substitutions, two of which were obtained in a screen for spindle pole body assembly defects and one of which increases RNAP II terminator recognition by S. pombe Seb1, a Nrd1 ortholog. All three caused NNS terminator readthrough in vivo and decreased RNA-binding affinity of the RBD in vitro. Surprisingly, the substitution with the most severe in vitro RNA-binding defect, G344D, exhibited readthrough of only a minority of snoRNA terminators affected by the original nrd1-5 substitution (V368G), which had the least severe RNA-binding defect. Transcriptome analysis showed that Nrd1-G344D caused dysregulation of mRNAs largely distinct from those affected by Nrd1-5 and identified a role for Nrd1-dependent termination in phosphate regulation similar to that of Seb1 in S. pombe. We conclude that the G344D and V368G substitutions in the RNA recognition motif distinguish between some of the diverse substrates of Nrd1.

works.title: Author Correction: Malonyl-CoA is a conserved endogenous ATP-competitive mTORC1 inhibitor
works.abstract: After publication, the authors were made aware of mistakes in the numerical Source Data files underlying Extended Data Figs. 3 , 5 , 8 . The errors arose from inadvertent copy-paste events during the transfer of quantified data between analysis files and the Source Data tables, affecting data presented in Extended Data Figs. 3 c, 5 c, 5 i, and 8d . The Source Data tables have been corrected, and the corresponding Extended Data figures and relevant figure legends have been updated in the HTML and PDF versions of the article. The corrected data have been verified against the underlying quantification data. Importantly, these corrections do not alter the conclusions of the study. The authors sincerely apologize for these errors. For comparison, the original figures are available as Supplementary Information accompanying this amendment.

works.title: Keratin 9 regulates mechanosensitive YAP1 signalling in palmoplantar epidermis
works.abstract: The palmoplantar epidermis, in adapting to the exceptional mechanical strain it bears during locomotion, is histologically and molecularly distinct from other skin body sites. The mechanisms specifying and maintaining its unique identity remain incompletely defined. Here we identify the type I keratin 9 (KRT9/K9), a protein uniquely expressed in palmoplantar epidermis, as a key modulator of mechanosensitive YAP1 signalling in response to postnatal mechanical compression. K9 loss-of-function variants driving KRT9-pEDD, a palmoplantar epidermal differentiation disorder, result in aberrant YAP1 subcellular partitioning and elevated levels of the stress-induced keratin 16 (KRT16/K16). Krt9 null mice recapitulate these molecular phenotypes as early as postnatal day 3. We further identify dynamic, YAP1-dependent regulation of Krt16/K16, upstream of and necessary for Krt9/K9 expression, during early postnatal development in situ and in response to mechanical compression of keratinocytes ex vivo, highlighting the role of mechanical stress in epidermal specification. Mechanistically, K9 interacts with the YAP1 binding protein 14-3-3σ and sequesters YAP1 in the cytoplasm, inhibiting its transcriptional activity; these functions are disrupted by KRT9-pEDD-causing variants in K9. Finally, we show that genetic or pharmacological inhibition of YAP1 ameliorates palmoplantar keratoderma in Krt9 null mice. These findings reveal a role for mechanical cues in specification and maintenance of palmoplantar skin and suggest new therapeutic interventions for inherited palmoplantar epidermal differentiation disorders.

works.title: Nonadhesive functions of E-cadherin promote cancer cell survival and metastasis
works.abstract: E-cadherin suppresses invasion and promotes metastasis in invasive ductal breast cancer, through suppression of reactive oxygen species (ROS). We sought to determine the cellular source of apoptosis-inducing ROS and to identify the domains of E-cadherin that are essential for cancer cell survival. Inhibition of mitochondria-derived ROS was sufficient to rescue cell death following E-cadherin deletion, in both 3D colony formation and in vivo metastasis assays. We next generated Cdh1 constructs by mutating amino acids or deleting domains, then tested their ability to rescue colony formation in E-cadherin-deleted cells. Surprisingly, E-cadherin constructs in which the extracellular domains were deleted, adhesion was compromised, or catenin interactions were blocked could rescue elevated mitochondrial ROS and 3D colony formation. Conversely, a construct lacking the cytoplasmic domain was unable to rescue ROS or cell death. Our findings reveal that E-cadherin's ability to regulate mitochondrial ROS, cancer cell survival, and metastatic outgrowth is separable from its role in intercellular adhesion.

works.title: Mechanically induced septin networks protect nuclear integrity
works.abstract: The cytoskeleton is a key mediator of mechanical interactions in cells, but specific contributions of septins remain unclear. Septins preferentially localize with a subset of actin stress fibers positioned under the nucleus, where they are situated between the membrane and stress fibers. Removing the nucleus from the cell results in the loss of these subnuclear septin-decorated stress fibers. Surprisingly, however, their formation can be rescued using a large glass bead in place of the nucleus. Similarly, applying a compressive force to the cell via confinement, whether externally or through internally generated actomyosin forces, results in increased septin accumulation in regions where the nucleus engages the cell cortex. Finally, loss of septin filaments via knockdown of SEPT7 increases nuclear membrane rupture during confinement. Together, these data argue that septins act as a dynamic mechanosensitive protective network to buffer mechanical forces on the nucleus.

works.title: Septins buffer actomyosin forces to protect the nucleus from genotoxic mechanical stress
works.abstract: Invasively migrating cells thread their nucleus through confined interstitial spaces. How cells protect the nucleus from intracellular forces is poorly understood. Here, we show that the septin cytoskeleton buffers the actomyosin forces that have been shown to power nuclear movement. Septin filaments comprising SEPT9, a septin amplified in breast cancer, align with perinuclear actomyosin cables, which exhibit higher tensile stress during 3D confined migration through narrower pores. SEPT9 depletion amplifies actin stress during confined migration and after myosin II hyperactivation in nonmigrating cells causing actin and nuclear envelope ruptures. Following confined migration, DNA breaks, nuclear blebs, micronuclei, and cell death increase in SEPT9-depleted cells, phenotypes rescued by the oncogenic SEPT9 isoform 1. Clinicogenomic data reveal that SEPT9 amplification associates with lower genomic alteration in aggressive breast tumors. We propose that septins are a mechanoprotective element of the cytoskeleton, and SEPT9 amplification enhances tumor cell survival by preventing nuclear damage.

works.title: Antiparallel dimerization of obscurin controls M-line assembly in Drosophila indirect flight muscle
works.abstract: The giant scaffold protein obscurin plays a crucial role in anchoring thick filaments at the muscle M-line. Here we show that Drosophila obscurin forms an antiparallel dimer at the M-line with the N-terminal SH3-DH-PH domain facing outwards toward the thin filaments, and the C-terminal kinase region involved in dimerization or oligomerization as well as myosin binding. This arrangement is supported by myosin co-immunoprecipitation, yeast two-hybrid, and super-resolution microscopy data, as well as Obscurin mutants specifically affecting the N- versus the C-terminus. While deletion of the N-terminal domains of obscurin predominantly affects peripheral thin filament length, loss of the C-terminal kinase region of obscurin disrupts early sarcomere assembly leading to various defects during sarcomere maturation, supporting its role in keeping thick filaments in register. In conclusion, we propose that obscurin forms a structural and elastic component organizing thick filaments with its C-terminal kinase region at the M-line, while connecting to thin filaments with its N-terminal domains.

works.title: Extracellular vesicles from chemoresistant breast cancer cells reprogram macrophages toward an M2-like phenotype in an ABCC1-dependent manner
works.abstract: Triple-negative breast cancer is characterized by high rates of chemoresistance and poor clinical outcomes. Although ATP-binding cassette (ABC) transporters are well-established mediators of drug efflux, their role in tumor-immune communication remains poorly defined. Here, we investigated whether the acquisition of doxorubicin resistance alters extracellular vesicle (EV) biogenesis and cargo content. We report that the doxorubicin-resistant MDA-MB-231 cell line exhibits significantly higher rates of EV production, without changes in particle size distribution, compared to the parental cell line. At the cellular level, we observed a significant increase in the number of multivesicular bodies present in doxorubicin-resistant cells. Proteomic and Western blot analysis of isolated EVs derived from the doxorubicin-resistant MDA-MB-231 cell line, compared to the parental MDA-MB-231 cell line, revealed an enrichment of ABCC1, accompanied by enrichment of vesicle-associated pathways. Cellular ABCC1 localized to CD63-positive compartments and was validated to be enriched in resistant cell line-derived EVs. Functionally, EVs from resistant cells promoted M2-like polarization of primary human macrophages, characterized by decreased CD86⁺ and increased CD206⁺ populations in addition to a decrease in IL-6, IL-8 and TNFα levels. Knocking down ABCC1 in resistant cells significantly attenuated this effect. Together, these findings suggest EV-associated ABCC1 might be a contributor to macrophage polarization and immune modulation in breast cancer.

works.title: GPI lipid remodeling regulates lipophagy in response to glucose deprivation
works.abstract: Lipophagy is an important microautophagic process that degrades lipid droplets (LDs) to mobilize stored lipids as an energy source during nutrient starvation. However, the molecular mechanisms regulating lipophagy in response to nutrient starvation remain poorly understood. We found that budding yeast mutants defective in glycosylphosphatidylinositol (GPI) lipid remodeling exhibited aberrant accumulation of lipid droplets (LDs), neutral lipids, and a reduced degradation of Faa4-GFP, a lipophagy reporter under glucose starvation. Furthermore, we demonstrated that glycosylphosphatidylinositol-anchored proteins (GPI-APs) localize to vacuoles in response to glucose depletion, and that a mutant defective in endocytosis has defects in lipophagy. These results imply that GPI lipid remodeling is required for lipophagy upon glucose starvation, and we propose that endocytosis functions to supply the lipid portion of GPI-APs, remodeled to C26 diacylglycerol, to the vacuolar membrane for lipophagy.

works.title: TGIF is a golgin-like protein required for Golgi structural maintenance and function in Toxoplasma gondii
works.abstract: The Golgi is an essential organelle that serves as a central hub for endomembrane trafficking. In the protozoan parasite Toxoplasma gondii, a single Golgi stack is essential for parasite survival; however, the molecular determinants governing Golgi structure and function remain poorly understood. Here, we characterize a Golgi-associated protein that is required for Golgi integrity and function, which we named Toxoplasma Golgi Integrity Factor (TGIF). Loss of TGIF disrupts parasite replication and natural egress and is lethal to the parasite. To investigate the impact of TGIF depletion on secretory protein trafficking, we adapted a fluorescence-based pulse-chase assay to monitor the synthesis and trafficking of microneme and rhoptry proteins. We found that loss of TGIF significantly impaired the synthesis and trafficking of microneme and rhoptry neck proteins, whereas trafficking of rhoptry bulb proteins was minimally affected. These findings suggest that rhoptry bulb proteins may traffic independently of canonical Golgi-dependent pathways. Collectively, our study provides new insight into the mechanisms of Golgi-mediated trafficking in T. gondii and identifies TGIF as a critical regulator of parasite secretory pathway organization and function.

works.title: The BAR domain-containing protein ciBAR1 requires Cby1 for efficient binding to phosphoinositide-enriched membranes to promote early ciliogenesis
works.abstract: Bin/Amphiphysin/Rvs (BAR) domain-containing proteins participate in membrane-remodeling processes, including vesicle trafficking, cell division, and cell migration. We previously demonstrated that ciBAR1 interacts with Cby1 and colocalizes at the ciliary base to promote ciliogenesis. However, the function of the Cby1/ciBAR1 complex remains poorly understood. Here, using recombinant proteins and reconstituted liposomes, we show that ciBAR1 alone exhibits little or no lipid-binding activity, whereas Cby1 promotes ciBAR1 binding to liposomes. In nanobar assays, Cby1 also promotes ciBAR1 membrane association and enrichment at regions of high membrane curvature. The Cby1/ciBAR1 complex preferentially associates with liposomes containing PI(4,5)P 2 and PI(3,4,5)P 3 , two phosphoinositides (PIs) enriched near the ciliary base. Consistent with these findings, ciBAR1 mutants defective in either membrane or Cby1 binding fail to localize to the ciliary base and are unable to rescue ciliogenesis defects in ciBAR1 -KO NIH3T3 cells. Furthermore, ultrastructural analysis reveals that ciBAR1 -KO cells exhibit defects in preciliary vesicle recruitment and an accumulation at the ciliary vesicle stage, suggesting impaired progression to ciliary membrane extension and ciliary bud formation. Collectively, our findings support a model in which Cby1 potentiates ciBAR1 binding to PI-enriched membranes at the basal body, where the Cby1/ciBAR1 complex mediates membrane-associated processes during early ciliogenesis.

works.title: Predicted structure of the complete CPLANE complex reveals novel interactors and mechanisms of Jbts17 during ciliogenesis
works.abstract: Cilia are highly conserved organelles that use hundreds of unique proteins to drive extracellular motility and serve as signaling hubs for eukaryotic cells. The Ciliogenesis and Planar Polarity Effector (CPLANE) protein complex controls basal body docking during early ciliogenesis and recruits the intraflagellar transport (IFT) proteins to the base of growing cilia. Leveraging recent advantages in deep learning neural networks and high-performance computing, we predict the structure of JBTS17, the largest CPLANE subunit, and the tertiary structure of the complete CPLANE complex, revealing direct contacts between JBTS17 and three other CPLANE members. We then used this model for an in silico protein-protein interaction screen that identified several novel JBTS17 interactors. Experiments in Xenopus confirmed a functional link in vivo between Jbts17 and the Spinocerebellar ataxia-associated protein TTBK2. The data provide new insights into mechanisms of CPLANE function during ciliogenesis and demonstrate the power of modeling protein complexes for the discovery of physical and functional protein interactions in cell homeostasis and disease.

works.title: A developmental resource mapping tubulin isotype deployment during corneal morphogenesis
works.abstract: Microtubules are core cytoskeletal polymers that support epithelial organization, polarity, and tissue morphogenesis. They are composed of α- and β-tubulin heterodimers encoded by multigene families that generate closely related but distinct isotypes. Although several tubulin isotypes have been implicated in ocular development and disease, their spatial organization during corneal morphogenesis remains poorly defined. Here we establish a resource visualizing and quantifying tubulin isotype localization during corneal development using the chick embryo. Comparative amino acid sequence analysis demonstrates that chick and human α- and β-tubulin isotypes are highly conserved within structural and catalytic domains, with divergence concentrated in C-terminal regions normally associated with post-translational modification sites. Relating sequence features to tissue organization, we performed longitudinal immunohistochemical analysis of five tubulin isotypes across corneal development. These analyses reveal distinct and dynamic patterns of isotype enrichment along apicobasal axes, as well as stage-dependent redistribution during epithelial maturation and endothelial differentiation. TUBA5/TUBA4A displays particularly restricted localization, including enrichment in migratory corneal stromal progenitors and the developing corneal epithelium and endothelium. Together, these data provide a conserved spatial framework for tubulin isotype organization during corneal morphogenesis and establish the chick embryo as a tractable model for investigating isotype-specific microtubule organization during epithelial development.

works.title: Programmable apoptosis circuits enable subtractive engineering of stem cell-derived organoids and embryoids
Leveraging genomic deep learning models for the prediction of noncoding variant effects
Genome-wide detection of genotype–environment interactions at biobank scale with fastGxE
works.abstract: Traditional genome-wide association studies have primarily focused on detecting main genotype effects, often overlooking genotype-environment interactions (GxE), which are essential for understanding context-specific genetic effects and refining disease etiology. Here we present fast genotype-environment interaction analysis (fastGxE), a scalable and effective genome-wide GxE method designed to identify genetic variants that interact with environmental factors to influence traits of interest. fastGxE controls for polygenic effects, polygenic interaction effects and noise heterogeneity; it remains robust to the number of environmental factors involved in GxE interactions; and it ensures scalability for genome-wide GxE analysis in large biobank studies, achieving speed improvements of 32.98-126.49 times over existing approaches. We illustrate the benefits of fastGxE through extensive simulations and an in-depth analysis of 32 physical traits and 67 blood biomarkers from the UK Biobank. In real-data applications, fastGxE identifies 7 genomic loci associated with physical traits, including 4 novel ones, and 18 genomic loci associated with blood biomarkers, 12 of which are novel. The new discoveries highlight the dynamic interplay between genetics and the environment, uncovering potentially clinically relevant pathways that could inform personalized interventions and treatment strategies.

works.title: Genome-wide analyses identify 60 loci associated with liver triglyceride content
works.abstract: Abstract We performed a large-scale genome-wide association study meta-analysis of magnetic resonance imaging-derived liver triglyceride content across 71,488 European-ancestry participants from the UK Biobank, approximately doubling the sample size of previous genome-wide association studies 1 . We identified 60 independent loci, including 31 not previously reported, and estimated the single nucleotide polymorphism-based heritability of liver triglyceride content at 25%. Integrative fine-mapping and gene-prioritization analyses nominated candidate effector genes for 48 loci. Of the 31 newly identified variants, 14 were validated in meta-analyses of clinically diagnosed metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (42,163 cases and 1,646,254 controls). People in the highest versus lowest decile of a polygenic risk score for liver triglyceride content had 2.71-fold higher odds of cirrhosis and 7.47-fold higher odds of hepatocellular carcinoma. Plasma proteins associated with the liver triglyceride polygenic risk score were enriched for metabolic remodeling and inflammatory pathways, with liver-enriched protein signatures increasing and visceral adipose signatures decreasing with higher genetic risk. Together, these findings refine the genetic architecture of liver triglyceride content, linking polygenic susceptibility to downstream metabolic and inflammatory pathways and providing insights into the genetic basis of steatotic liver disease.

works.title: Why cells use many lipids when few will do
The Vizitig pangenome and pantranscriptome explorer
works.abstract: Vizitig is the first platform for real-time exploration and querying of DNA and RNA sequence de Bruijn graphs across many samples, unifying visualization, metadata, and flexible search. It constructs compacted colored de Bruijn graphs from raw sequencing reads and reference sequences and then provides an interactive web interface for graph exploration. It integrates raw and reference-based data, handles complex variation, and provides a human-readable feature-based (also referred to as metadata) query language with scalable graph loading. Its domain-specific query language supports composable searches combining sequences of arbitrary size, genomic features such as gene or exon identifiers, and experimental factors such as sample identifiers or abundance thresholds. On-demand subgraph loading retrieves only regions of interest, enabling interactive exploration of large data sets in the graphical user interface without loading the entire graph into memory. We demonstrate Vizitig's capabilities through case studies in pantranscriptomics and pangenomics. In pantranscriptomics, we recover fusion transcript breakpoints on long and short reads. In pangenomics, we explore sequence variations across yeast, rice, nematode, and human pangenomes. Vizitig scales from small virus genomes to human-scale pangenomes (our largest experiment comprises up to 20 assembled human haplotypes, on a laptop). Vizitig enables fast, reproducible analysis in both pangenomics and pantranscriptomics while providing a deployable and user-friendly working environment.

works.title: Base composition reflects RNA polymerase II displacement
works.abstract: RNA polymerase II (Pol II) transcribes all protein-coding and many non-protein-coding genes in the genome. Pol II transcription termination is crucial for RNA maturation and, when disrupted, can lead to altered RNA processing and RNA export. Termination involves two intertwined processes: RNA cleavage and Pol II release from the DNA (displacement). Despite its importance, the exact mechanisms underlying Pol II displacement from the DNA remain poorly understood. Moreover, under certain cellular stress conditions, there is a partial failure of cleavage, leading to a shift of the position of displacement further downstream, a phenomenon known as readthrough transcription. We present a systematic analysis of Pol II termination across cell types and species and provide novel insights into the mechanism of displacement. Using a probabilistic mixture model to quantify Pol II dynamics across entire gene bodies from nascent RNA sequencing data, we find that genes fall into two classes defined by conserved base composition patterns near the displacement site. Both classes share a T-rich region upstream of displacement, and one class additionally carries a GC-rich region surrounding displacement. We find that GC-rich predisplacement regions have more accessible chromatin and higher levels of phospho-threonine 4 on the CTD of Pol II. Additionally, we find that displacement at genes with only the upstream T-rich pattern are more likely to be affected by perturbations that alter displacement, including heat shock, viral infection, kinase inhibition, and arsenic treatment. Thus, our work identifies two types of Pol II displacement regions, which are differentially affected by perturbations of cellular homeostasis.

works.title: Inter-individual gene expression variability implies stable regulation of brain-biased genes across organs in three ray-finned fishes
works.abstract: Phenotypic variation among individuals provides the raw material for evolution, and gene expression is a key mediator between genetic and phenotypic variation. As for phenotypes, the range of gene expression is limited and biased by evolutionary and developmental constraints. Observed expression variability due to biomolecular stochasticity and cell-to-cell heterogeneity has been well-studied in isogenic populations of unicellular organisms. However, for multicellular organisms with a diversity of cells and tissues sharing the same genetic background, the interplay between expression variability, gene and organ function, and gene regulation remains an open question. Here, we use highly multiplexed 3'-end bulk RNA sequencing to generate transcriptome profiles spanning at least nine organs in outbred individuals of three ray-finned fish species: zebrafish, Northern pike, and spotted gar. Per organ, we quantify individual-to-individual gene expression variability independent of mean expression level. Lowly variable genes are enriched in cellular housekeeping functions whereas highly variable genes are enriched in stimulus-response functions. Furthermore, highly variable genes evolve under weaker purifying selection at the protein-coding sequence, indicating that intra-species expression variability predicts inter-species protein sequence divergence. Genes that are broadly expressed across organs are both highly expressed and lowly variable, whereas organ-biased genes are typically highly variable within their top organ. Among organ-biased genes, patterns of expression variance are dependent on the top organ. Specifically, brain- and gonads-biased genes have lowly variable expression across different organs, suggesting stabilizing selection. These patterns suggest that gene regulatory mechanisms evolve under organ-specific selective pressures.

works.title: Refining indel- and structural variant-trait associations with LAVrefiner
works.abstract: Structural variants (SVs) are major sources of human genetic diversity. Despite advances in SV discovery, most single-nucleotide polymorphism (SNP)-centric frameworks overlook sequence-level information and encode overlapping variants as independent features, potentially reducing power in association studies, biasing heritability estimation, and limiting prediction accuracy. Here, we present LAVrefiner, a scalable, sequence-aware method that decomposes overlapping sequence-resolved SVs and indels into nonoverlapping refined sequence components and generates genotype matrices compatible with standard SNP-based analyses. In tandem repeat (TR) regions, LAVrefiner further supports motif-aware allele comparison and repeat copy-number estimation. When applied to variants from the 1000 Genomes Project, LAVrefiner identifies 224,708 refined variants. Simulations show that LAVrefiner is fast and memory-efficient while maintaining robust genotype representations under TR-associated sequencing noise. In gene expression analyses, models combining LAVrefiner-derived copy-number estimates with refined variants yield the highest heritability estimates and prediction accuracy in short tandem repeat (STR) and variable number tandem repeat (VNTR) regions, outperforming models based on the original SV/indel representation and existing TR copy-number tools. Cis -expression quantitative trait locus ( cis -eQTL) mapping further shows that refined variants can localize regulatory signals to specific sequence components, including an independent VNTR-derived signal at the TFRC locus. Together, LAVrefiner provides an efficient, context-aware strategy for integrating sequence-resolved SVs and indels into existing genetic analysis frameworks.

works.title: BioSIFTR: functional inference from shallow shotgun sequencing using biome-specific genome catalogues benchmarked in gut microbiomes
works.abstract: Abstract Shallow shotgun sequencing is an accurate microbiome profiling method, but its use for functions is limited. BioSIFTR extrapolates shallow shotgun read mapping to precalculated pangenome functions in 15 MGnify biome-specific catalogues, which span host-associated and environmental microbiomes. We benchmarked BioSIFTR on synthetic communities and on three gut microbiomes — red junglefowl, mouse, and human — using matched deep shotgun and 16S rRNA metabarcoding data, outperforming similar approaches. Further validation will require matched benchmark datasets and is a priority for future work. BioSIFTR is thus a practical method for functional inference from cost-effective shallow shotgun sequencing, currently validated in gut microbiomes.

works.title: Lipid-fuelled synaptic plasticity: integrating membrane turnover, β-oxidation, and protein lipidation
works.abstract: Synaptic plasticity requires the coordinated regulation of membrane remodelling, energy production, and protein turnover. However, how these processes are integrated at the molecular level remains unclear. Here, we propose that activity-dependent lipid flux represents a central mechanism linking these processes. Saturated free fatty acids (sFFAs) released from membrane phospholipids, triglycerides, or from extracellular uptake can be activated to acyl-CoA and directed to mitochondrial β-oxidation and synaptic protein lipidation. These represent two emerging pathways adding to the complexity of roles played by sFFAs, including membrane fluidity and receptor activation. Recent work identifies DDHD2 as a mechanistic entry point into this broader synaptic lipid network. We position DDHD2-dependent lipid mobilisation in the wider context of glia-neuron lipid transfer and ApoE/sortilin-dependent fatty acid uptake. Key unresolved questions include the source and fate of fatty acids, the relative contribution of β-oxidation versus glycolysis to ATP production, and whether these pathways are altered in neurodegenerative disease.

works.title: Activator mimicry by PP6 regulatory subunits directs Aurora A dephosphorylation in mitosis
works.abstract: Aurora A kinase is a conserved regulator of mitotic spindle assembly whose activity must be precisely balanced to ensure genome stability. Its activation at centrosomes and spindle microtubules is promoted by CEP192, TACC3 and TPX2, and counteracted by protein phosphatase 6 (PP6), which dephosphorylates the Aurora A T-loop. PP6 forms three holoenzymes defined by regulatory subunits PPP6R1-R3, yet how these confer substrate recognition and regulation is poorly understood. Here, we identify a phenylalanine-rich motif (A-box), present in PPP6R2 and PPP6R3 but absent from PPP6R1, that binds a surface on Aurora A overlapping those used by CEP192, TPX2 and TACC3. Mutation of A-box phenylalanine residues disrupts Aurora A binding and T-loop dephosphorylation, elevating spindle-associated Aurora A activity, and enlarging mitotic spindles. PPP6R2 additionally contains a unique PLK1-docking site downstream of its A-box, explaining how PLK1 competes with Aurora A for PPP6R2 and thereby suppresses PP6 activity towards Aurora A. Together, these findings show that PP6 regulatory subunits mimic Aurora A activators to direct dephosphorylation, and reveal how competing interactions regulate PP6 in mitosis.

works.title: Non-random inter-speckle material transfer mediated by dynamic multiphase interchromatin connections
works.abstract: Nuclear speckles (NS) enhance the expression of NS-associated genes, possibly by elevating local levels of factors involved in multiple steps of gene expression. While dozens of large NS are distributed throughout interchromatin regions, the extent to which NS components dynamically redistribute between NS to adjust to local physiological demands remains unknown. Here, we used live-cell imaging of endogenous NS proteins to identify an interchromatin network of connections that functionally link NS throughout the nucleus. Over timescales ranging from tens of seconds to minutes, NS material is transferred through these curvilinear connections, rather than through isotropic exchange across the NS/nucleoplasm interface followed by diffusion in all directions throughout the nucleoplasm as predicted by current models. Multiphase NS-connecting structures form through the dynamic juxtapositions of multiple NS component phases. Each phase exhibits distinct yet recurrent dynamic patterns, but together, they integrate into a more stable, multiphase, NS-connecting structure in an ATP- and transcription-dependent manner. Our findings reveal the existence of a cellular mechanism that facilitates coordinated inter-NS protein trafficking through multiphase connections.

works.title: DZIP3 is a viral RNA co-sensor for RIG-I that promotes type-I interferon responses
works.abstract: RNA-binding E3 ubiquitin ligases have the ability to link RNA regulation to the protein ubiquitination machinery, thereby influencing diverse biological processes. Here, we identify the RNA-binding E3 ubiquitin ligase DZIP3 as an innate immune sensor that couples viral RNA recognition to downstream immune signaling. Upon viral infection, binding of viral RNA to the DZIP3 RNA-binding motif induces conformational changes that promote K63-linked auto-ubiquitination, oligomerization, and stabilization of DZIP3. Activated DZIP3 associates with RIG-I and MAVS at the mitochondrial membrane, promoting K63-linked ubiquitination of RIG-I and robust activation of the type-I interferon response. Consequently, DZIP3 depletion impairs host antiviral defense, whereas DZIP3 restricts infection by a broad range of RNA viruses. Our findings establish DZIP3 as an innate immune co-sensor that integrates viral RNA detection with ubiquitin-mediated signaling, revealing a regulatory mechanism of RIG-I-MAVS-mediated antiviral immunity.

works.title: Meta-analysis of over 8,000 individuals from Hawai‘i and Samoa for genetic associations to cardiometabolic phenotypes
authors: Lifestyle and Genetic Adaptations (OLaGA) Study Group The Samoan Obesity
Lifestyle and Genetic Adaptations (OLaGA) Study Group The Samoan Obesity
works.abstract: Although genome-wide association studies (GWAS) now routinely reveal genetic associations and biological insights in millions of individuals, underrepresentation of global populations, such as those from Polynesia, continue to persist. These exclusions, often driven by logistical challenges and lack of data, prevent systematic identification of population-enriched associations, such as the association of the missense variant at the CREBRF locus to BMI and type 2 diabetes discovered commonly occurring in Polynesian populations due to its rarity in global populations. Armed with the recently updated TOPMed imputation panel that could benefit studies in diverse populations that previously had poorer imputation performance, we performed the first GWAS of Native Hawaiians and Samoans, the largest to date of Polynesian-ancestry populations (combined N up to 8,461) to identify population-enriched associations for 13 adiposity and cardiometabolic traits available across both cohorts: BMI, fasting glucose, fasting insulin, HDL, height, hip circumference, HOMA-IR, LDL, T2D, total cholesterol, triglycerides, waist circumference, and waist-hip ratio. We found 25 trait-loci associations that met genome-wide significance: 20 previously reported or known associations and 5 putatively new associations via meta-analysis. In particular, with improved statistical power, we were able to confirm the previously suggestive association between the missense CREBRF variant with fasting glucose levels. The remaining 4 potentially novel loci-trait associations for BMI, LDL, and waist-hip ratio, however, were not replicated in All-of-Us. The lack of Polynesian-enriched findings outside of the CREBRF locus informs the bounds of the effect sizes or frequencies of any enriched variants and suggests that further expansion of cohort sizes from this region of the world and improved imputation references specific to these populations are needed to identify more population-enriched associations.

works.title: The role of gene regulatory evolution in weapon diversification: Insights from comparative genomics, chromatin profiling, and functional analyses of BMP signaling in horned beetles
works.abstract: Condition-responsive growth is a common feature of multicellular development, during which organisms integrate genetic and environmental signals to adjust their phenotype. However, the molecular properties shaping condition-responsive diversification remain poorly understood. The beetle genus Onthophagus offers promising opportunities to investigate this question, given its diversity of sex- and nutrition-responsive phenotypes, including horns - novel, secondary sexual weapons used in reproductive competition. We compared the gene regulatory properties of horns in two closely related species exhibiting highly specialized sex- and nutrition-biased phenotypes. We found a dynamic cis-regulatory landscape in developing horn tissue, shaped by mutational accumulation across species, condition-specific changes in chromatin accessibility within species, and the acquisition of lineage-specific regulatory elements. Many of these putative regulatory regions include binding site motifs of critical developmental regulatory genes, including members of the bone morphogenetic protein signaling pathway. We provide functional evidence that two proteins in this pathway have been co-opted for horn development, influencing the shape and size of this trait across species, sexes, and nutritional states. These findings provide evidence that evolutionarily labile cis-regulatory interactions may evolve alongside diversification of condition-specific traits, potentially modifying the activity of conserved developmental pathways over short evolutionary timescales.

works.title: Simpler is not always better: Phylodynamic misspecification and deep-learning corrections
works.abstract: Phylodynamics bridges the gap between epidemiology and pathogen genetic data. The birth-death (BD) model and its extensions serve to infer the average number of secondary infections Re and the infection duration d from time-scaled pathogen phylogenies. Moreover, more complex models add extra parameters, such as the average length of the incubation period, the proportion of superspreaders in the infected population, or the speed-up in detection after contact-tracing. However, these additional parameters come at an important computational cost: While the simplest, BD, model, has a closed-form solution, its extensions do not and require numerical methods for their likelihood computation. This leads to increased computational times and potential numerical errors. Therefore, the BD model remains the favorite researchers' choice for real dataset analyses, and is often applied even in cases where more complex epidemiological aspects are present. We investigated, using simulations, how model misspecification influences inference of Re and d in the phylodynamic framework. We showed that the use of models not accounting for various epidemiological aspects leads to bias. In particular the simplest, BD, estimator tends to underestimate Re in the presence of super-spreading, incubation or contact-tracing, which might be dangerous from the public health perspective. In contrast, deep-learning-based estimators for complex models, accounting for multiple epidemiological factors, performed well in our simulations both on the data where those factors were present and where they were absent. This motivates the use of complex epidemiologically realistic estimators, whose design has recently become possible thanks to deep learning.

works.title: A domesticated totivirus-like tandem array undergoes interspecific transfer and asymmetric evolution
works.abstract: Functional genes derived from nonretroviral RNA viruses are generally expected to evolve more slowly following integration into host genomes. Here, we characterize Scheffersomyces totivirus-like open reading frame repeat module (STORM), a tandem array of four totivirus-derived ORFs (TLC1 to TLC4) maintained in wood- and insect-associated yeasts for at least 15 My. STORM has nevertheless accumulated greater amino-acid divergence than sampled exogenous totiviruses. Host-calibrated rate analyses estimated that STORM evolved approximately 7-fold faster than related exogenous viral lineages. Evolution within the array was asymmetric. RELAX identified strong gene-wide relaxation in TLC4 (K = 0.29), whereas BUSTED detected no episodic positive selection. Despite this relaxation, TLC4 retained predicted decapping-associated residues, with evidence of purifying selection at several positions. Structural predictions indicated that STORM proteins retain a totivirus-like architecture, and RNA-seq comparisons revealed paralog-specific expression. Among 3,527 complete nuclear gene trees, none recovered all relationships defining any of the three STORM discordances with strong support, indicating that these patterns are exceptional relative to the nuclear genomic background. Local synteny and preservation of the four-copy array further support three interspecific transfers. In the best-supported transfer, STORM was flanked by an ATP10 pseudogene and a transposase pseudogene from yeast endogenous element transposon (YEET), a newly identified Tc1/mariner-like transposon family. Both pseudogenes grouped phylogenetically with the inferred donor clade, and YEET1a-like terminal inverted repeats at the locus were characteristic of that clade. STORM therefore illustrates the selective maintenance, rapid asymmetric evolution, and horizontal mobility of a nonretroviral paleoviral array.

works.title: Unilateral cross-feeding constrains adaptive evolution, even in the producer without direct fitness effects
works.abstract: Cross-feeding interactions are pervasive in microbial communities and profoundly shape community structure, stability, and function. While previous studies have explored how cross-feeding affects evolvability, this work has predominantly focused on bidirectional mutualistic interactions in engineered auxotrophic systems where both partners reciprocally exchange essential metabolites. However, most metabolic interactions in natural microbial communities are unidirectional, with organisms feeding on the metabolic waste products of other species. Our study addresses this gap by examining how a unidirectional cross-feeding interaction affects the evolutionary dynamics of both the producer (Acinetobacter johnsonii) and consumer (Pseudomonas putida) over 800 generations of experimental evolution. We found that co-culture constrained adaptive evolution in both species. Co-cultures exhibited lower πN/πS ratios (0.75 for P. putida; 1.04 for A. johnsonii) than monocultures (1.44 and 2.02, respectively), indicating stronger purifying selection against nonsynonymous mutations in the community context. Lineage tracking through whole genome sequencing of populations and clones revealed greater lineage diversity and complexity in monocultures, with more mutations showing significant parallelism across replicate populations. Additionally, P. putida evolved increased dependence on its partner; co-culture-evolved P. putida grew significantly worse than its ancestor when A. johnsonii was removed. These findings indicate that ecological interactions can reshape fitness landscapes and constrain adaptive evolution even when fitness benefits are unidirectional, with implications for understanding microbial community stability and predicting evolutionary dynamics in complex communities.

works.title: Recent geographic dispersal and environmental adaptation of indica rice
works.abstract: Rice (Oryza sativa), one of the key domesticated cereal crops, is comprised of several subspecies or variety groups. A major variety group, O. sativa var. indica, was domesticated in the Indian subcontinent ∼4,500 years ago via introgression of domestication alleles from var. japonica and today represents the predominant rice that is grown worldwide, particularly in tropical and subtropical regions in Asia. Using genome data from 957 indica landraces, including 194 newly re-sequenced cultivars and 38 herbarium specimens collected over the last 167 years, we reconstruct how indica rice moved from the Indian subcontinent to other parts of Asia. Unlike japonica rice, indica rice seems to have dispersed relatively recently (within the last 2,500 years) to China, mainland and island Southeast (SE) Asia. Interestingly, we find that the island SE Asia indica rice landraces show gene flow with island SE Asian japonica landraces. We also find significant gene-environment associations of indica rice with local climatic and edaphic variables that may be linked with local adaptation and possible cultural selection for grain quality traits.

works.title: Meeting gene expression demand during evolution of antibiotic resistance
works.abstract: Regulated gene expression in bacteria accommodates demands imposed by different environments. In addition to ensuring the production of required metabolic and structural components, gene regulation protects bacteria against the adverse effects of misexpression. Upon encountering a novel environment, such as sustained exposure to antibiotics, transcriptional recalibration ensues to improve fitness. For antibiotics, this involves enhancing the expression of an existing repertoire of resistance mechanisms and is often mediated by mutations in regulators of gene expression. Here, we review how diverse gene regulatory mutations confer antibiotic resistance to bacterial pathogens. We view these strategies through the lens of the Gene Expression Demand Theory, originally proposed for inducible operons involved in sugar metabolism, and describe the molecular basis and evolutionary consequences for a few well-studied examples. Broad underlying preferences of when and which kind of regulatory mutations bacteria employ emerge from these examples. A key pattern appears to be a preference for derepression rather than activating mutations, and we highlight potential underlying genetic and evolutionary explanations. Finally, even as our knowledge of molecular mechanisms of antibiotic adaptation continues to expand, we propose that adaptation by regulatory mutations provides a framework for assessing the risk of resistance evolution in the case of novel antibiotics and alternative targets for diagnostic and therapeutic interventions.

works.title: Correction: Sperm entry without genome inheritance: incorporate or exclude—egg-intrinsic control of paternal genome fate in Cobitis fish
Pseudouridylation landscape across 42 nuclear-encoded S. cerevisiae tRNAs
works.abstract: Pseudouridine is the most abundant RNA base modification due to its prevalence in tRNA and rRNA, where it serves as a key modulator of structure and function. Yet, in the widely used model organism, the budding yeast Saccharomyces cerevisiae , tRNA pseudouridine sites have not been comprehensively annotated. Here, we performed two high-throughput methods established for detecting tRNA pseudouridylation positions: Nanopore direct RNA sequencing (DRS) and 2-bromoacrylamide-assisted cyclization sequencing (BACS). Using DRS, we sequenced cytosolic tRNA from seven pseudouridine synthase (PUS) knockout S. cerevisiae strains , including deletion strains of Pus1, Pus3, and Pus7. Analysis of these data verified thirty-two existing pseudouridine annotations and predicted an additional ten previously unannotated pseudouridine sites. Our analysis also revealed DRS signal changes at several non-uridine sites with the loss of a PUS, including apparent changes in modification abundances at position 37 upon deletion of Pus3. Liquid chromatography tandem mass spectrometry (LC-MS/MS) and primer extension assays, however, indicated no change in the abundance of these modifications with the loss of Pus3, underscoring the need for caution in interpreting DRS-based signal changes. Using BACS, we confirmed the ten DRS-predicted novel sites, while further detecting eleven additional previously unannotated pseudouridine sites. Combining existing modification annotations from the Modomics database with our DRS and BACS datasets, we created a map of all detected pseudouridines—totaling 126 sites, including 21 novel sites—and the enzymes responsible for their catalysis, across the forty-two nuclear-encoded S. cerevisiae tRNA isoacceptors.

works.title: The rise of reducing reagent-resistant TfR1 dimer marks ferroptosis
works.abstract: Ferroptosis is an iron-dependent type of cell death caused by excessive membrane lipid peroxidation. It remains a challenge to detect ferroptotic cells, especially in in vivo settings, hindering translational studies. Here we discover that a reducing reagent-resistant (3R) dimer of the transferrin receptor 1 (TfR1) is a highly specific indicator for lipid peroxidation. The 3R dimer is elevated in cells when ferroptosis is induced, either by pharmacological agents or by genetic perturbations. Furthermore, the 3R dimer can be used to detect disease-associated ferroptosis in tissue and in extracellular vesicles isolated from mouse or patient plasma. Given the near-ubiquitous expression of TfR1, we posit that the 3R dimer may function as a ferroptosis marker with widespread potential utility for basic and translational studies. He et al. report the upregulation of a reducing reagent-resistant form of the transferrin receptor 1 dimer during lipid peroxidation and demonstrate its utility in detecting ferroptosis in tissue lysates and extracellular vesicles from mice and humans.

works.title: The N-Ank protein Ankrd24 shapes neurons and couples to syndapin and the F-actin promoter Cobl-like
works.abstract: Proper neuromorphogenesis is pivotal for neuronal network formation and brain function. The underlying cell biological tasks are complex, as they include both remodeling of membrane topologies and of cytoskeletal structures. Yet, mechanisms coordinating these two different cell biological functions are largely unknown. Here, we molecularly and functionally characterize ankyrin repeat domain-containing protein 24 (Ankrd24) and demonstrate that this ankyrin-repeat protein is able to interact with and bend membranes and mechanistically and functionally belongs to the recently proposed N-Ank superfamily. Mutational analyses revealed that the N-Ank functions of Ankrd24 are indispensable for Ankrd24's role in neuromorphogenesis. Ankrd24 furthermore physically cooperated with the F-BAR domain protein syndapin I (PACSIN1) and with Cobl-like (Cobll1), a protein promoting actin filament formation, by ternary complex formation. Both partners were critical for Ankrd24-mediated dendritic arborization. This identified Ankrd24 as critical part of a larger, coordinated effort in inducing new dendritic branches. Our work thereby sheds light on the molecular mechanisms underlying the complex task of proper neuronal arbor development.

works.title: First person – Kei Takahashi
works.abstract: First Person is a series of interviews with the first authors of a selection of papers published in Journal of Cell Science, helping researchers promote themselves alongside their papers. Kei Takahashi is first author on ‘ Cross-species molecular mapping of the photoreceptor sensory cilium and periciliary structures identifies conserved and species-specific architectural features’, published in JCS. Kei is a postdoc in the lab of William A. Beltran at the University of Pennsylvania, USA, working on advanced microscopy and molecular approaches to investigate the nanoscale architecture of photoreceptors and how this is altered in retinal disease.

works.title: Phase separation of Rbpms sequesters translation elongation machinery to preserve hematopoietic stem cell function
A self-organized tri-lineage bone model in liquefied microcapsules captures matrix dynamics in early remodeling
Multiancestry conditional and joint analysis applied to GWAS summary statistics
works.abstract: Conditional and joint (COJO) analysis of genome-wide association study (GWAS) data is a standard post-GWAS analysis for identifying statistically independent associations. Although GWAS meta-analyses are increasingly conducted across multiple ancestry groups, the optimal strategy for multiancestry COJO analysis remains unclear. Here we introduce Manc-COJO, a method for multiancestry COJO analysis. Simulations and real-data analyses show that Manc-COJO improves detection of independent association signals while reducing false positives compared with single-ancestry COJO implemented in genome-wide complex trait analysis (GCTA) and its ad-hoc multiancestry adaptations. We also introduce Manc-COJO:FIX, a follow-up algorithm to identify ancestry-specific independent associations. The C++ implementation of Manc-COJO is over 120-fold faster than GCTA-COJO and supports linkage disequilibrium references derived from either individual-level genotype data or pre-computed matrices, facilitating analyses when data sharing is limited.

works.title: A systems perspective on monoallelic inborn errors of immunity
Imputation of fluid intelligence to increase power for gene discovery
The landscape of gene loss and missense variation across the mammalian tree informs on gene essentiality
works.abstract: Abstract Patterns of gene and sequence preservation across species provide insight into gene essentiality under natural selection.
